days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride along the Bay of Kotor with beautiful views of the bay, then continue towards the Adriatic coast and descend along the coastal road to Bar through serpentine sections and open sea views.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Climb inland from the coast through hilly terrain, with smooth bends and mountain views, finishing in Podgorica.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: The **Durmitor Ring** is an officially promoted scenic loop around Durmitor National Park, starting and ending in Žabljak on narrow, paved mountain roads. It includes high‑altitude passes such as Sedlo, wide alpine meadows, and dramatic views over the Tara Canyon. The character of the route is tight, winding single‑lane pavement with steep gradients and frequent viewpoints, offering classic high‑mountain riding with minimal traffic and strong national‑park scenery.

points.name: Mala Crna Gora area viewpoint on Tara Canyon near Ćurevac
Mala Crna Gora area viewpoint on Tara Canyon near Ćurevac

days.title: Day 1
days.description: The **Ibar Highway** is one of Serbia’s best-known motorcycling roads, running southwest from Belgrade toward western Serbia and onward toward Montenegro. It combines long rural stretches, river valleys, and steady curves with heavier traffic in some sections. The road is widely recognized as a major touring corridor through central and western Serbia, with changing scenery from the Belgrade approach to the more mountainous interior.

title: Sarajevo - Konjic - Jablanica - Mostar (Neretva Canyon Route, M17)
subtitle: A 1-day tour of Bosnia and Herzegovina

days.title: Day 1
days.description: This is the classic **Neretva River canyon** route on main road M17, connecting Sarajevo with Mostar via Konjic and Jablanica. The road is fully paved, with a mix of flowing curves, tunnels, and river‑side sections as it follows the emerald Neretva. It combines mountain scenery, reservoirs, and historic towns, with Mostar’s old bridge area as a natural end point for the day.

title: P14 Scenic Road - Plužine to Žabljak (Durmitor National Park)
subtitle: A 1-day tour of Montenegro

days.title: Day 1
days.description: The **P14 road** between Plužine and Žabljak is one of Montenegro’s most renowned mountain drives, climbing from the deep Piva canyon and lake up to the Durmitor plateau. The paved road is narrow and twisty, carved into cliffs with frequent tunnels and balcony‑style sections overlooking turquoise Piva Lake. As it approaches Žabljak, the route opens to high‑mountain scenery, meadows, and views of Durmitor peaks, making it a compact but very intense day ride.

points.name: Piva Lake viewpoint near Mratinje direction
Piva Lake viewpoint near Mratinje direction

title: Lovćen Serpentine - Cetinje to Kotor (Lovćen National Park)
subtitle: A 1-day tour of Montenegro

days.title: Day 1
days.description: The **Lovćen route** runs from the historic royal town of Cetinje into Lovćen National Park, then descends to the Bay of Kotor via the famous serpentine road. Above Lovćen, the pavement winds through forest and karst with panoramic views, including access to the Njegoš Mausoleum. The descent to Kotor features a series of tight hairpins stacked above the fjord‑like bay, widely regarded as one of Montenegro’s classic motorcycling roads for scenery and riding challenge.

points.name: Mausoleum of Njegoš, Lovćen National Park
Mausoleum of Njegoš, Lovćen National Park

title: Adriatic Coastal Road - Bar to Budva
subtitle: A 1-day tour of Montenegro

days.title: Day 1
days.description: The **Adriatic coastal section** between Bar and Budva runs on the main seaside road, combining tunnels, short climbs, and descents with frequent sea views. The pavement is standard highway quality, with curves around headlands and access to beaches and small seaside towns. Despite being relatively short, this segment is a classic coastal ride in Montenegro, offering Mediterranean scenery, old towns, and the option to stop at overlooks above the coastline.

title: Skadar Lake Ride - Virpazar to Rijeka Crnojevića and Cetinje
subtitle: A 1-day tour of Montenegro

days.title: Day 1
days.description: This **Skadar Lake route** connects Virpazar on Lake Skadar with Rijeka Crnojevića and onward to Cetinje via narrow, winding tarmac. The road above the lake offers balcony‑style sections, small villages, and viewpoints over the characteristic wetlands and meanders. From Rijeka Crnojevića to Cetinje the ride continues on twisty secondary pavement through hilly terrain, combining rural landscapes with access to the historic capital.

title: Moraca Canyon Road - Podgorica to Kolašin (E65/E80)
subtitle: A 1-day tour of Montenegro

days.title: Day 1
days.description: The **Moraca Canyon section** of the E65/E80 between Podgorica and Kolašin is a major but scenic mountain road following the Morača River. The route uses engineered pavement with tunnels and bridges, frequently cut into steep canyon walls with river views below. Traffic is heavier than on minor mountain roads, but the combination of significant elevation change, gorge scenery, and sweeping curves makes it a notable Montenegro ride.

points.name: Morača Monastery area in Morača Canyon
Morača Monastery area in Morača Canyon

title: Kotor - Petrovac - Podgorica - Mojkovac - Đurđevića Tara - Žabljak
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Montenegro

days.title: Day 1
days.description: This **multi‑day loop** is a well‑known composite route linking the Adriatic coast at Kotor and Petrovac with inland Podgorica, then heading north through Mojkovac to the Đurđevića Tara Bridge and Durmitor. It combines coastal riding, central‑Montenegro valleys, and high‑mountain scenery.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: The character shifts from busier coastal highways to quieter mountain roads and dramatic canyon sections, culminating with the famous Tara Bridge and the Durmitor area around Žabljak.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: The final leg reaches the Durmitor area around Žabljak.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: The **Zlatibor-Sjenica** road crosses a high plateau in western Serbia and is a well-known scenic motorcycling corridor. The road is paved, open, and generally fast, but the landscape feels remote and elevated. Riders pass through rolling mountain country, open grasslands, and colder upland terrain, making it one of Serbia’s most recognizable inland touring routes.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: The **Kopaonik route** links the town of Brus with the Kopaonik mountain area and down toward Raška on mountainous paved roads. It features steady elevation gain, forested slopes, and alpine-style terrain by Serbian standards. This is a strong choice for mountain riding, with cool-weather conditions at higher elevations and multiple access points into the national park.

points.name: Kopaonik National Park / Pančić’s Peak access area
Kopaonik National Park / Pančić’s Peak access area

days.title: Day 1
days.description: The **Đerdap Gorge** route follows the Danube through Đerdap National Park, one of Serbia’s most famous scenic roads. It combines river views, cliff sections, and long sweeping stretches along the Iron Gates. This is a major touring ride with excellent natural scenery and strong historical interest, especially around Golubac and the archaeological area near Lepenski Vir.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: The **Tara Mountain** road climbs from Bajina Bašta onto the Tara plateau on curving forest roads. It is a compact mountain route with dense woodland, viewpoints, and access to one of Serbia’s best-known overlooks. The riding is slower and more technical than main highways, but the combination of forest, elevation, and canyon viewpoints makes it a standout scenic loop.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: The **Fruška Gora loop** is a popular road ride in northern Serbia, linking Novi Sad with the historic town of Sremski Karlovci and the wooded Fruška Gora hills. The roads are paved and generally easy, with a mix of wine-country scenery and gentle climbs. It is less alpine than Serbia’s southwestern routes, but it offers a compact and accessible ride with cultural stops and light mountain curves.

points.name: Fruška Gora ridge viewpoint near Iriški Venac
Fruška Gora ridge viewpoint near Iriški Venac

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Stuttgart on smaller B-roads heading southwest toward the northern Black Forest, avoiding the busy Autobahn where possible. The run to Freudenstadt via routes like the B295 and B28 gives you flowing curves through mixed forest and farmland, with good pavement and frequent villages for fuel and coffee stops.

From Freudenstadt, continue on the SchwarzwaldhochstraГџe (B500), one of GermanyвЂ™s classic motorcycle roads, with sweeping bends, elevation changes, and wide views over the Rhine valley when the weather is clear. The last leg to Triberg is tighter and more enclosed, following forested valleys with occasional rougher sections and sharper bends that reward precise riding.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Head south from Triberg through Furtwangen on winding secondary roads that roll over low ridges and through quiet villages. Traffic is generally light, though local trucks and buses use these roads, so corner visibility and careful overtakes are important.

The section around Titisee-Neustadt offers lakeside scenery and holiday traffic, but excellent asphalt with a mix of fast sweepers and tighter bends. Continue toward Todtnau via roads such as the B31 and L126, climbing into higher forested terrain with more pronounced elevation changes, occasional hairpins, and viewpoints over the valleysвЂ”ideal for spirited yet controlled riding.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
From Todtnau, tackle the ascent toward the Feldberg area, one of the highest paved regions in the Black Forest, via narrow, winding roads with significant elevation gain and frequent hairpins. The pavement is good but can have forest debris or damp patches, especially in the morning, so ride with caution in shaded corners.

Drop down toward Schluchsee along sinuous lakeside roads with pleasant rhythm and scenic water views. The final stretch to Waldshut-Tiengen follows rural routes parallel to the Rhine, a mix of rolling farmland and forest with smoother, more relaxed curves, making for a comfortable end to the Black Forest loop.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Climb back into the forested hills from Waldshut-Tiengen toward Bonndorf on smaller L-roads, with narrower carriageways and occasional rough patches but engaging corners. Traffic is mostly local, offering extended stretches of uninterrupted riding through dense woods and meadows.

Continue to Sankt Blasien and then west toward LГ¶rrach, weaving through valleys on a mixture of B-roads and local routes. Expect frequent elevation changes, some tight village entries, and occasional roadworks. The final approach to LГ¶rrach is more urban but still avoids the main motorway, finishing the day with a relaxed pace.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Leave LГ¶rrach on secondary roads along the edge of the Rhine plain, passing through vineyards and small towns around MГјllheim. The terrain is gentle, with broad, sweeping bends and typically excellent asphalt, allowing a relaxed warm-up before heading back toward the Black Forest edge.

From MГјllheim to Freiburg, choose smaller roads parallel to the main B3 to keep clear of heavy traffic, then head northeast to Stuttgart via the B-road network, avoiding long Autobahn stints where possible. The ride back includes a mix of faster rural sections and occasional forested stretches, closing the loop with varied riding without being overly demanding.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Depart Munich on smaller regional roads heading south, skirting the busy Autobahn to reach Bad TГ¶lz. The ride quickly transitions from urban sprawl to rolling countryside, with well-paved two-lane roads and moderate traffic. Bad TГ¶lzвЂ™s old town makes a pleasant stop before continuing toward the foothills.

From Bad TГ¶lz to Lenggries, follow the Isar valley on winding roads with gentle elevation changes and frequent curves. The scenery becomes more alpine, with forested slopes and distant peaks, while the road surface remains mostly excellent, occasionally narrowing in village sections.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride south from Lenggries toward Sylvenstein Reservoir along a scenic river valley, with flowing curves and good visibility. The reservoir area offers dramatic water and mountain views, and the roads can be busy on weekends with cars and bikes, so expect occasional slow-moving traffic.

Continue west toward Kochel am See and over the KesselbergstraГџe, a famous twisty climb with tight bends, notable elevation changes, and sections requiring disciplined speed control. After descending, make your way to Garmisch-Partenkirchen on mixed B-roads with sweeping alpine vistas, finishing in a mountain town with full services.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Leave Garmisch on curving mountain roads to Ettal and Oberammergau, both connected by scenic routes through forested hills and small passes. Pavement is generally good, though narrower sections and tourist coaches demand extra caution, especially in peak season.

Head onward toward FГјssen via small alpine villages and lakeside roads, choosing the quieter B-roads over the main highways. Approaching FГјssen, the landscape opens to broad views of the Alps and castles, with a mix of sweeping corners and occasional hairpinsвЂ”an enjoyable but not overly strenuous riding day.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Explore small roads around FГјssen and WeiГџensee, where narrow lanes wind between lakes and hills. These routes can have uneven surfaces, tight turns, and local traffic, making them more technical but rewarding for riders comfortable with slower, precise cornering.

Continue to Pfronten and then north toward Kaufbeuren on rural highways that cut through dairy country and gentle hills. The pavement improves and the curves relax, offering an easier rhythm after the tighter morning sections, with ample opportunities for short stops in village squares.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Ride from Kaufbeuren to Landsberg am Lech along secondary routes parallel to the river, where broad curves and well-maintained asphalt make for a comfortable cruise. The old town of Landsberg offers cobbled streets and cafГ©s ideal for a mid-day break.

From Landsberg back to Munich, avoid the autobahn where practical by following regional roads through farmland and small towns. The dayвЂ™s riding is less demanding, concluding the alpine loop with a relaxed run into the city.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Hamburg heading northwest on smaller routes parallel to the A27, crossing the flat, wind-swept landscapes of Lower Saxony. The roads are mostly straight but can be exposed to strong crosswinds, with occasional long, gentle curves and good pavement.

Approach Cuxhaven along rural roads close to the coast, then continue to Bremerhaven via the B73/B6 corridor, choosing side roads where possible to keep traffic down. Expect occasional industry and port traffic near Bremerhaven, but the riding remains manageable with clear signage and frequent fuel stops.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Follow the coast north from Bremerhaven through Wremen and Dorum-Neufeld on local roads that run close to dike lines and marshland. These roads are mostly narrow, with occasional rough sections and agricultural vehicles, requiring steady attention.

Cross the Weser and head toward BГјsum, using secondary routes instead of motorway segments to keep the ride engaging. The scenery is dominated by flat fields, dikes, and glimpses of the sea, with long sightlines and minimal elevation changes, ideal for relaxed cruising at moderate speeds.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Ride north from BГјsum toward Husum on quiet coastal roads, passing through small fishing and farming communities. The asphalt is generally good but can have windblown sand or salt residue near the water, so braking points demand awareness.

Continue to St. Peter-Ording via roads along the Eider estuary and coastal dunes. The route offers expansive views, straight stretches broken by gentle curves, and frequent chances to stop on or near the beaches. Traffic can be heavier near holiday areas but remains manageable with patient riding.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Depart St. Peter-Ording through TГ¶nning, using smaller inland roads to vary the scenery, with more trees and villages than the open coastal sections. The roads are mostly wide two-lane routes with smooth surfaces and gentle curves that allow for relaxed, steady speeds.

From Heide, head back toward Hamburg on regional roads, avoiding long autobahn runs. The final approach into Hamburg becomes busier and more urban, with junctions and traffic lights, so fatigue management and situational awareness are important at the end of the coastal tour.

title: Saxon Switzerland and Elbe Valley Ride
subtitle: A 4-day tour of Germany

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Dresden on smaller roads following the Elbe River toward Pirna, where you transition from urban streets to more scenic riverside routes. The pavement is generally good, with gentle curves and moderate local traffic.

Continue south to Bad Schandau in the heart of Saxon Switzerland, where roads tighten and begin to undulate more noticeably through sandstone rock formations and forest. Expect narrower sections, occasional rough patches, and tourist traffic, making smooth, controlled riding essential.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Explore the Saxon Switzerland region with a loop through KГ¶nigstein and Sebnitz, riding narrow, twisty roads that weave between cliffs and forest. Many sections have sharp bends and limited visibility due to rock faces and trees, so corner entry speeds must be conservative.

Push on to Hinterhermsdorf on lightly trafficked routes that feel almost like secret backroads, with variable pavement quality. The mixture of tight turns, short straights, and scenic viewpoints offers a highly engaging but physically demanding riding day.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Depart Hinterhermsdorf on smaller roads to Neustadt in Sachsen, then to Bischofswerda, riding through rolling countryside with a patchwork of fields and woods. The roads widen and become less technical, with smoother asphalt and gentler curves, offering a welcome contrast to the previous day.

From Bischofswerda back to Dresden, follow secondary highways that avoid major high-speed sections but still allow for efficient travel. Traffic increases as you approach Dresden, with more junctions and urban riding, so attention to traffic flow and navigation is important.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Take a shorter loop along the Elbe upstream to MeiГџen, using riverside roads lined with vineyards and historic villages. The curves are gentle but frequent, with generally excellent pavement and occasional cobbled sections in older town centers.

Return via Radebeul and back into Dresden on minor roads through wine country. This day is less demanding, focusing on smooth, scenic riding with plenty of opportunities to stop and enjoy viewpoints over the river and hills.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Hannover on regional roads toward Hildesheim, avoiding the autobahn and using smaller highways that cut through fields and gentle hills. The roads are wide, well-paved, and moderately trafficked, making for a calm start to the tour.

From Hildesheim, ride southeast toward Goslar, entering the foothills of the Harz Mountains. Curves become more frequent and the road profile more varied, with gradual climbs and descents. GoslarвЂ™s historic center is a good base for the night, with easy access to mountain routes.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Head into the Harz highlands via Clausthal-Zellerfeld, riding narrow, curvy roads through dense forest and past reservoirs. Pavement is generally good, though some sections can show wear from winter, so watch for cracks and repaired patches.

Continue through Altenau to Braunlage, using routes with notable elevation changes, hairpins, and sweeping bends. These roads are popular with riders and can get busy on weekends, but they remain highly enjoyable if you manage pace and traffic.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Ride from Braunlage to Sankt Andreasberg on very twisty, climbing roads with tight hairpins and steep gradesвЂ”a highlight for experienced riders who enjoy technical mountain riding. Surface quality is mostly good, but occasional gravel in corners demands caution.

Descend toward Bad Lauterberg and then to Nordhausen along smaller B-roads and local routes that roll through valleys and forest. Curves relax somewhat, and traffic is light, making for a pleasant but still engaging day in varied terrain.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Return north through the eastern Harz ridges toward Bad Harzburg via rural highways and forest roads. The first half of the day still offers elevation changes and longer curves, with good asphalt and modest traffic.

From Bad Harzburg, head back to Hannover on regional roads, skirting major motorways while still making efficient progress. The landscape flattens out, and the riding becomes more relaxed, closing the Harz loop without excessive fatigue.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Depart Munich south on secondary roads toward Rosenheim, avoiding the busy A8 where possible. The ride traverses gently rolling Bavarian countryside with wide, well-paved roads and frequent villages, ideal for warming up before reaching the mountains.

Continue to the border near Kiefersfelden and cross into Austria toward Kufstein using the local border crossing, where traffic is heavier but manageable. Roads in this area offer more elevation variation and a mix of sweeping curves, though some sections are busier due to transit traffic.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride east from Kufstein through Walchsee and across the border back into Germany toward Reit im Winkl on scenic lake and valley roads. The pavement is generally excellent, with flowing bends, modest elevation changes, and light traffic outside holiday peaks.

From Reit im Winkl, head toward Berchtesgaden on mixed B-roads with increasingly dramatic mountain scenery. Expect tighter curves, occasional hairpins, and some narrower sections with limited passing opportunities, rewarding smooth and attentive riding.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Leave Berchtesgaden toward Bad Reichenhall and cross the border into Austria near Schneizlreuth, following river valleys with long sweepers and good asphalt. Traffic includes local trucks and buses, so overtakes should be planned carefully.

From Lofer to Zell am See, the route follows the Saalach and then the valleys around the lake, with more pronounced elevation changes and scenic views. The roads feature a mix of faster curves and occasional tight bends, with some exposed sections near drop-offs that require confident cornering and focus.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
From Zell am See, head west toward Mittersill and then northeast toward KitzbГјhel, riding through high alpine valleys on well-paved main routes with occasional passes. Curves are frequent but generally wide, with sections allowing a steady, flowing pace.

Continue to Kufstein on scenic valley roads with moderate traffic and good surfaces, rejoining familiar territory near the border. This leg offers sustained mountain vistas without being overly technical, a fitting close to a cross-border alpine run.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave SaarbrГјcken northeast on smaller roads through Sankt Wendel, passing wooded hills and farming villages. Pavement is mostly smooth, with a mix of gentle curves and short straights, and traffic is light outside commuter hours.

Continue west toward Trier along the Moselle valley on secondary roads that hug the river, with more pronounced curves and occasional narrow sections in villages. The scenery features vineyards climbing the slopes above the river, making for engaging yet relaxed riding.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride from Trier to Saarburg and Merzig, largely following the Saar River on minor roads. Expect a pleasant mix of river bends, valley views, and small towns, with decent pavement and modest traffic.

From Merzig, cross into France near the border at Apach and head to Metz using regional roads, avoiding main autoroutes to keep the ride interesting. French rural highways offer sweeping curves, good surfaces, and occasional roundabouts, requiring consistent observation of signage and varying speed limits.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Depart Metz north toward Thionville on secondary routes along the Moselle, with broad curves and well-maintained asphalt. Traffic is moderate but generally smooth-flowing, with occasional industrial zones near river ports.

Cross back into Germany near Perl and follow rural roads to SaarbrГјcken, tracing parts of the Moselle and Saar valleys. The last stretch includes a mix of wide sweepers and urban entries, closing a cross-border loop with varied scenery and riding styles.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Berlin heading north on secondary roads toward Prenzlau, passing through the flat, lake-dotted landscapes of Brandenburg. The roads are wide, mostly straight, and well surfaced, with occasional gentle curves and low traffic.

From Prenzlau, continue northeast toward the Oder River and cross into Poland at the border near Mescherin, heading to Szczecin. Approach the city via smaller access roads to avoid heavy motorway traffic, navigating more complex junctions but maintaining manageable speeds.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride east from Szczecin on regional roads toward GoleniГіw and Nowogard. These Polish highways are generally well paved with long straights and occasional broad curves, though some sections can show surface repairs that warrant attention.

Continue to KoЕ‚obrzeg on the Baltic Sea, using roads that gradually become more coastal and touristic. Traffic increases near the seaside, but the riding remains comfortable, with occasional tree-lined stretches and glimpses of the sea.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Head east along the Baltic coast toward Koszalin on mixed highways and smaller connectors, avoiding the busiest express routes where possible. The terrain is flat but wooded, with a mix of gentle bends and straights, yielding a moderate, steady pace.

Continue to SЕ‚upsk on similar roads, where short urban sections alternate with longer rural stretches. Pavement is generally good, though occasional potholes or repaired sections can appear on smaller connectors.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Turn inland toward BytГіw and Chojnice, entering the Kashubian lakes region with more varied terrain. Roads become more curvy and occasionally narrower, weaving between forests and lakes, which adds riding interest and requires closer attention in blind bends.

Traffic is light, and surfaces are mostly reasonable, though some rural stretches may show wear and occasional gravel near junctions. The day offers sustained scenic, moderate-speed riding through low hills and water-rich landscapes.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Ride through the Tuchola Forest area toward Tuchola, where roads are often lined with dense pine woods and feature gentle, flowing curves. Pavement is mostly good, though some smaller roads can be narrower and slightly rough.

Continue to Bydgoszcz on regional highways that balance efficiency with riding interest, finishing the cross-border tour in a larger Polish city with full services. The final stretch remains manageable, with typical urban traffic patterns near the destination.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Depart Chemnitz on regional roads toward Zwickau, riding through low hills and mixed industrial and rural areas. The roads are mostly wide and well surfaced, with moderate traffic and frequent junctions that require attentive navigation.

Continue southwest to Plauen, skirting larger highways in favor of B-roads that offer more curves and elevation changes. The terrain becomes more undulating, with increasingly scenic views over valleys and fields.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
From Plauen, ride south toward Adorf/Vogtland and cross into the Czech Republic near the border around Bad Brambach/Cheb. The roads on both sides of the border are generally good, but some Czech rural sections may show more surface variations and patched areas.

Head to Karlovy Vary via curving valley roads that follow rivers and cut through forested hills. Expect a mixture of sweeping bends and tighter corners, with occasional narrow sections and limited shoulder space, rewarding smooth cornering technique.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Explore the region around Karlovy Vary and Loket on scenic country roads that trace the OhЕ™e River and surrounding hills. These routes feature regular curves, short climbs, and descents, with mostly good asphalt but some rough patches in smaller villages.

Continue south to MariГЎnskГ© LГЎznД› on gently twisting roads through forests and spa towns. Traffic varies but is rarely heavy; however, tourist areas may have more pedestrians and parked cars, requiring extra care when passing through town centers.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Ride north toward the German border, crossing near Waldsassen. The route passes through rolling countryside with a mix of forest and farmland, and roads are generally well paved with low traffic. Some sections have gentle but frequent curves that keep the ride engaging.

Continue to Weiden in der Oberpfalz on secondary highways, avoiding longer autobahn segments. The riding becomes more relaxed as the landscape flattens slightly, with broad curves and good visibility, making for a comfortable final day on this loop.

title: Lake Constance to Swiss Alpine Edge
subtitle: A 4-day tour of Germany

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Konstanz and ride north along the shore of Lake Constance to Meersburg on scenic lakeside roads. These routes are relatively narrow and can be busy with tourist traffic, but they offer frequent curves, pleasant views, and generally good asphalt.

Continue to Friedrichshafen via shoreline roads and short inland diversions, with gentle elevation changes and occasional tight village corners. Traffic is moderate, especially in summer, so smooth, patient riding is important.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride east along the northern shore of Lake Constance to Lindau, following minor roads close to the water where possible. The route features a mix of straight sections and soft curves, with good surfaces but frequent town entries and speed changes.

From Lindau, continue to Bregenz, crossing the border into Austria near the end of the lake. Urban traffic increases near the towns, but the distances are short and the roads straightforward, with the lake always close by as a visual reference.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
From Bregenz, ride south through Hohenems on valley roads at the foot of the Alps, where the terrain becomes more dramatic but the roads remain broad and well paved. Curves are longer and more sweeping, with occasional tighter sections near villages.

Cross into Switzerland near AltstГ¤tten and continue to St. Gallen via regional roads that climb gently through farmland and forest. The surfaces are generally excellent, with consistent radius corners and good visibility, offering satisfying, smooth riding.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Ride north from St. Gallen to Romanshorn, descending toward Lake Constance on secondary roads that pass through villages and agricultural land. Expect gentle curves and well-marked junctions, with low to moderate traffic.

Follow the southern shore of the lake back toward Konstanz, crossing the border to Germany near Kreuzlingen. The lakeside stretch combines pleasant views, smooth asphalt, and frequent small towns, bringing the cross-border loop to a calm and scenic finish.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Oslo on secondary roads through the eastern side of the Oslofjord, where the riding is a mix of urban exits, lakeside edges, and increasingly open coastal scenery. Pavement is generally excellent, with moderate traffic around commuter zones and smoother flow once you are outside the capital.

The run to Moss and then Fredrikstad is not especially technical, but it has a pleasant touring rhythm with gentle curves, ferry-port activity, and easy access to the shoreline. Expect occasional roundabouts and speed changes, but the day stays relaxed and practical for a loaded motorcycle.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Head southeast from Fredrikstad on smaller county roads toward Halden, riding through low-lying farmland and forest. The roads are mostly well surfaced and lightly trafficked, with a few narrow stretches and local junctions that reward steady attention.

From Halden, continue inland toward Ørje on rural roads with more frequent bends and a quieter, more remote feel. This is a classic southeastern Norway day: modest elevation changes, dense forest, and a calm pace rather than dramatic mountain riding.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Ride north from Ørje toward Kongsvinger on pleasant inland roads that combine open farmland with forest corridors. The pavement is usually good, though some sections can feel narrow by international touring standards, and you will share the road with local traffic and agricultural vehicles.

Continue to Elverum on broad regional roads with long, flowing curves and limited congestion. The riding is efficient rather than demanding, but the scenery of wooded hills and river valleys keeps the day engaging for a motorcycle traveler.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
This is a longer inland day into the high plateau country, with roads that gradually become more open, cooler, and more sparsely populated. Expect smooth asphalt on main regional roads, but also long stretches with few services, so fuel planning matters.

The approach to Tynset and Røros brings more elevation, bigger skies, and a distinctly northern feel. Curves are generally broad, but wind exposure can be noticeable, and some sections may have rougher winter wear; the historic mining town of Røros makes a strong overnight stop.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Leave Røros on quieter inland roads, riding through rolling uplands and forested valleys where traffic is light and the sense of isolation is high. The road character is straightforward, but the scenery is broad and atmospheric, especially in changing light and weather.

The route back toward Elverum is steady and practical, with a mix of long straights and easy curves rather than technical mountain passes. It is an efficient final day for an interior Norway loop, best enjoyed at a measured pace with attention to weather and wildlife.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Bergen and head inland toward Voss on roads that climb gradually away from the city and quickly become more scenic. The route is well known for its flowing curves, tunnel sections, and frequent changes in elevation, with traffic that can build around weekends and holidays.

From Voss to Eidfjord, the riding becomes more dramatic, with fjord-side scenery, mountain walls, and roads that repeatedly bend with the terrain. Expect tunnels, occasional narrow sections, and strong visual payoff, especially where the road opens to views over water and cliffs.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Follow the Hardangerfjord corridor west and south, using ferries or bridge connections where needed, with a route that feels designed for motorcycle touring. The roads vary between smooth, faster valley sections and tighter shoreline stretches where the terrain forces sharper bends.

The Hardanger Bridge area and the roads toward Utne and Odda provide some of Norway’s most memorable fjord riding, with steep slopes, waterfalls, and a mix of tunnels and open viewpoints. Watch for tourist traffic, especially near popular stops and ferry landings.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Climb out of Odda into higher mountain territory toward Røldal, where the road gains elevation quickly and the bends tighten. The surface is generally good, but weather can change rapidly and shaded sections may stay damp longer than expected.

Continue toward Sauda on a route with a stronger alpine feel, including narrower roads, steeper gradients, and occasional exposed stretches. This is a rewarding riding day for experienced motorcyclists who enjoy mountain terrain and careful line choice.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Leave the mountains behind and head toward the coast, where the roads become broader and less demanding but still scenic. The ride includes fjord crossings, some ferry-dependent segments, and a mix of rural roads with light traffic.

The final run into Stavanger is more urban, but the approach still offers coastal views, small islands, and a steady touring rhythm. Compared with the mountain days, this stage is easier and faster, giving you a good balance across the route.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Bodø and head south and east through coastal Nordland, where the road feels remote and the scenery is dominated by sea inlets, mountains, and open sky. The pavement is generally good, but long sightlines can lull riders into complacency, so watch for wildlife and sudden weather shifts.

This first day is about rhythm rather than complexity, with a mix of gentle bends and occasional tighter sections near fjord arms. Traffic is usually light, making it easy to settle into a calm touring pace.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride north and west through northern coastal Norway, using a combination of roads and ferry crossings that are essential to the region’s travel pattern. The route is not fast in the highway sense, but it is rich in scenery and constantly changing conditions.

The Lofoten approach is one of the most dramatic motorcycle days in the country, with steep mountains, fishing villages, bridges, and narrow coastal roads. Expect tourist traffic in summer and possible wind exposure on exposed bridge sections.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Spend the day on the classic Lofoten road network, where every segment feels scenic. Roads are generally paved and well maintained, but they can be narrow, busy with camper traffic, and interrupted by bridges, short tunnels, and village speed limits.

The riding itself is a mix of easy curves and very short technical sections, especially near the coastal settlements. It is less about speed and more about the constant visual drama of peaks, water, and fishing harbors.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Continue south through the western end of Lofoten, where the road becomes narrower and more intimate, threading between mountains and sea. The surface is usually good, but the road geometry and local traffic require full concentration.

Reine and Å are among the most photogenic stops in Norway, but the riding remains the main attraction: short straights, quick transitions, and frequent opportunities to stop for photos or weather checks. This is a compact day that still feels full and memorable.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Turn northeast and make a longer run toward Narvik, mixing coastal roads, bridge links, and inland valleys. This is a more transit-oriented day, but the route still retains strong riding character thanks to changing scenery and a generally quiet road network.

The roads are mostly well surfaced, though sections may be narrow or affected by wind and rain. Narvik provides a practical destination with services, while the approach offers long-distance Arctic touring atmosphere rather than technical mountain riding.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Depart Oslo toward Drammen and Kongsberg on roads that start urban but quickly open into river valleys and forested lowlands. The riding is smooth and practical, with good pavement and moderate traffic around the main towns.

This is a gentle introduction to Telemark-style touring, with broad bends, easy gradients, and frequent places to stop. It is not a highly technical day, but it sets up the deeper interior roads to come.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride west into the mountain valleys toward Notodden and then Rjukan, where the road follows water and climbs into more dramatic terrain. Expect a strong mix of tunnels, curves, and steep-sided valley scenery.

The approach to Rjukan becomes distinctly alpine in feel, with tighter roads and more attention required in shaded or damp sections. This is one of the better days for riders who like a road to feel carved into the landscape.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Climb away from Rjukan into higher country toward Haukeli, where the road becomes more exposed and weather-sensitive. This area can change quickly in wind, fog, or rain, so even in summer it can demand extra caution.

The riding is excellent for motorcycles, with long sweepers, elevation changes, and mountain views that open and close as you cross the highlands. Some sections can feel remote, so fuel planning and weather awareness are important.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Descend into softer Telemark terrain, where lakes, farms, and forest roads create a calmer riding rhythm. The roads are generally in good condition, with a mix of gentle bends and rolling hills rather than dramatic mountain passes.

Seljord and Bø offer a more relaxed side of the region, but the routes remain enjoyable for a motorcycle because of their smooth flow and changing scenery. Traffic is usually moderate and easy to manage.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Head east toward Skien and Porsgrunn on easier roads that still preserve a touring feel through lakes and low forested hills. The final leg toward Oslo becomes more populated, with increasing junctions and commuter traffic.

This closing day is more about a smooth return than technical riding, but it ties the Telemark loop together well. The road network is straightforward, the scenery remains pleasant, and the gradual transition back to the capital gives the tour a logical finish.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Trondheim and head southwest toward Orkanger before turning toward the coast. The roads are mixed but generally well paved, with fjord-side sections, some tunnel passages, and moderate traffic near the larger settlements.

The route to Kristiansund is scenic and practical, with bridges, ferry connections, and a classic Norwegian rhythm of water crossings and shoreline riding. Curves are mostly moderate, making the day accessible without being dull.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride inland from Kristiansund toward Sunndalsøra, where the terrain becomes steeper and more enclosed by mountain walls. Roads are typically good but can feel narrow in places, with frequent tunnels and sections where water, rock, and road run very close together.

Continue to Oppdal through a valley corridor that offers long views and a steady series of bends. This is a satisfying day for riders who enjoy changing gradients and a strong sense of moving from coast to interior.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Push east across the inland plateau on roads that feel spacious, quiet, and remote. The riding is not highly technical, but there are long distances between settlements, so it helps to keep an eye on fuel and weather.

The approach to Røros adds a historic and atmospheric finish, with open terrain and increasingly cooler highland conditions. The road surface is usually decent, though early or late season travel may encounter rougher patches or lingering debris.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
This is a substantial northbound day through inland and valley roads, with the route chosen for flow rather than high speed. Expect a mix of broad curves, long straights, and sections where the landscape alternates between forest, river, and upland terrain.

The ride is more about distance and scenery than twisty excitement, but the roads are suitable for a touring motorcycle and usually lightly trafficked. Keep an eye on changing weather, especially in exposed interior stretches.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Continue north toward the coast, where the road begins to incorporate more ferry and bridge logic and the scenery turns distinctly maritime. The riding is calm but interesting, with fjord edges, wooded hills, and frequent changes in light and weather.

The final run to Brønnøysund offers a classic coastal Trøndelag feel, with moderate traffic and good pavement interspersed with slower sections near villages and ferry terminals. It is a practical, scenic end to a broad regional loop.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Oslo and head east toward Kongsvinger on inland roads that are straightforward and well surfaced. The route is mainly about efficient progress through forest and farmland, with light traffic once you clear the capital region.

Cross into Sweden at Charlottenberg, using a practical border crossing that suits road touring. The riding remains easy and organized, with gentle curves and clear signage, making it a simple and realistic international start.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride southeast through Sweden on broad regional roads toward Karlstad, where the landscape opens into lake country and flatter terrain. The roads are generally smooth and less technical than Norway’s mountain routes, but they still offer pleasant touring pace and good visibility.

Continue to Örebro on efficient secondary highways, avoiding a motorway-heavy day where possible. Expect steady traffic, numerous roundabouts, and long rural stretches, all of which make for a calm but substantial day in the saddle.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
This is a longer transit day through central and southern Sweden, where roads are typically wide, well maintained, and less curved than in Norway. The ride is best approached as a steady touring leg rather than an aggressive motorcycle stage.

Approaching Kalmar, the road network becomes more coastal, with bridges, open farmland, and intermittent views of the Baltic. It is a practical, realistic day for crossing a large part of southern Sweden before turning back toward Norway’s southern border.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Ride west through Småland on roads that pass forests, lakes, and small towns, with enough curves and surface changes to keep the day interesting. Traffic is moderate, and the pavement is usually excellent on main regional routes.

The run to Gothenburg is a substantial but manageable day, with the final approach becoming more urban and busy. For motorcyclists, the reward is a clear westward trajectory across Sweden that keeps the route logical and achievable.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Leave Gothenburg and ride north along the Swedish west coast toward Strömstad, where the landscape turns coastal and more rugged. The roads are generally smooth but can be busy near holiday areas and ports, so patience is useful.

Cross back into Norway at Svinesund on the E6 corridor and continue to Moss on a route that balances coastal views with efficient travel. This final international day is practical rather than technical, with good pavement and straightforward border infrastructure.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Bodø on the E6 corridor southward, a road that mixes efficient long-distance travel with broad scenic sections and tunnel passages. The riding is mostly straightforward, but the dramatic landscape keeps it engaging, especially as mountains and fjords frame the route.

The day to Mosjøen and Mo i Rana is more about endurance touring than technical riding, though the road surface is usually good and the traffic manageable. Expect variable weather and long gaps between major services in places.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Head east toward the border with Sweden using a long, realistic touring stage through northern Scandinavia. The route is dominated by open space, forest, and long-distance road sections that reward steady pacing and weather awareness.

Cross into Sweden and continue to Umeå, where the riding becomes more settled and urban near the end. This is a substantial day, but it is plausible on the region’s main roads and keeps the border-crossing logic straightforward.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Travel inland through Swedish Lapland on roads that are largely straight, smooth, and sparsely populated. The appeal here is not tight cornering but the vastness of the forest landscape and the sense of remoteness.

The route to Lycksele and Arvidsjaur is well suited to a loaded touring bike, with good visibility and consistent pavement. Wildlife caution is important, especially at dawn and dusk when moose and deer can appear unexpectedly.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Continue east and northeast across northern Sweden toward the Gulf of Bothnia, following roads that remain simple but long and remote. The surfaces are usually good, though shoulders can be narrow and weather can shift quickly.

Approaching Boden and Haparanda, traffic increases slightly and the landscape becomes more open. The border-town feel of Haparanda makes it a logical staging point for the final push back into Norway.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Cross from Sweden into Finland at the Haparanda–Tornio area and continue north through Finnish Lapland. The roads are typically well maintained, with long straight stretches, light traffic, and a very calm riding atmosphere.

Finish in Rovaniemi on broad northern highways that are easy to follow but exposed to weather and wildlife. This route is a realistic international end point that emphasizes long-distance northern touring rather than mountain riding.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Stavanger and ride north along the western coast, using roads that blend fjord crossings, tunnels, and coastal settlements. The route is not especially fast, but it is highly varied and suits a touring motorcycle well.

The approach to Bergen is scenic and often busy, with a mix of shoreline curves and traffic near larger towns. Good road quality and strong visual interest make it a satisfying first day on Norway’s west coast.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Head inland from Bergen toward Odda, then continue into higher mountain territory. This day introduces steeper gradients, more tunnel sections, and roads that follow narrow valleys with impressive waterfall and fjord scenery.

The approach over the high country is a classic Norwegian motorcycle experience, with changing weather and the possibility of cooler temperatures even in summer. It is important to be prepared for damp pavement and reduced visibility in mountain sections.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Descend toward southern Norway on a long but realistic touring day, using main roads that remain engaging thanks to hills, forests, and intermittent river valleys. The route is more about covering ground than seeking tight curves, but it stays motorcycle-friendly throughout.

The final approach to Kristiansand becomes more urban, with increasing traffic and junctions. It is a sensible place to rest before the international crossing the next day.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Cross from Norway to Denmark by ferry from Kristiansand to Hirtshals, which is the practical and realistic way to make this transition for a motorcycle tour. The riding after disembarkation is easy, with flat, well-marked Danish roads and minimal elevation change.

Continue to Aalborg on smooth regional highways that favor steady progress over technical challenge. Compared with Norway, the roads are straighter and less dramatic, but they are efficient and comfortable after the ferry leg.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Ride south through Denmark on broad, well-maintained roads that are ideal for relaxed touring. The landscape is flatter, traffic is more consistent, and the route becomes a straightforward country-crossing stage.

The day ends in Kolding, a practical destination with good services and easy onward access. It is a logical contrast to Norway’s fjords and mountains, giving the route a clear international character.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Tromsø and head east through northern Norway on long-distance roads that are scenic but demanding in terms of concentration. The route includes fjord edges, mountain passes, and long stretches where services are sparse.

The riding is straightforward rather than technical, but the scale of the landscape is immense and the weather can be changeable. Road surfaces are usually adequate, though some sections may feel remote and exposed to wind.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Continue east across Finnmark on roads that feel truly northern, with vast open spaces, long straights, and light traffic. This is a day where endurance and attention matter more than cornering technique.

The landscape shifts between plateau, river valley, and forest, and the road quality is generally good enough for comfortable touring. Wildlife and weather remain the main considerations on this remote stretch.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Cross into Finland near the border and continue south through Lapland on quiet roads with very little congestion. The terrain is subdued but beautiful, with forests, lakes, and broad horizons.

Finnish roads here are well suited to long-distance riding, with smooth pavement and predictable geometry. The challenge is not complexity but staying alert over long, sparsely populated distances.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Ride southwest toward Rovaniemi and then Kemi on easy-flowing Lapland roads. The day is mechanically simple but very pleasant for touring, with open forest, occasional rivers, and a quiet riding atmosphere.

Traffic remains low outside towns, and the road network is straightforward. This is a good day to preserve energy and enjoy the vastness of northern Finland before the final approach.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
The final day is short and practical, keeping the route within the 3–7 day rule while finishing in a different country. The road to Oulu is smooth, direct, and suitable for a relaxed arrival after several long northern stages.

While not technically demanding, the ride retains strong touring value through its coastal and forested northern scenery. Oulu offers a sensible endpoint with full services and a clear cross-border finish.

title: Southern Coast to Sweden and Backroads
subtitle: A 5-day tour of Norway

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start on Norway’s southern coast with a relaxed day along coastal roads and small towns. The route is easy to ride, with good pavement, mild curves, and plenty of opportunities to stop near harbors and beaches.

Traffic is moderate near the larger towns, but the overall pace is calm and suitable for settling into a multi-day trip. It is more about atmosphere than challenge, with the sea frequently in view.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride west back through Kristiansand and then continue toward the Oslofjord region, favoring secondary roads where possible to avoid a motorway-heavy feel. The route combines coastal and inland segments, with varied but manageable traffic.

This is a practical repositioning day with enough scenery to stay interesting, especially as the road moves through forested sections and port towns. Pavement quality is generally strong, and the riding remains relaxed.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Head inland and cross into Sweden, using roads that gradually transition from coastal Norway to inland forest and lake country. The route is well suited to a touring motorcycle, with broad curves and mostly smooth asphalt.

Crossing near Kongsvinger gives you a realistic border transition before continuing to Karlstad. The riding is steady and uncomplicated, with long rural stretches that favor endurance over technical skill.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Ride west through Sweden toward the Norwegian border, using roads that are mostly broad, efficient, and lightly curved. The landscape is a mix of forest, lake, and farmland, and the route remains easy to follow throughout.

Cross back into Norway near Halden and settle into the more varied terrain of southeastern Norway. The final miles are straightforward, with a good balance of touring flow and border-crossing practicality.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Finish the tour with a simple run back toward Oslo through the southeast corner of Norway. The roads are well maintained and efficient, with enough bends and small-town riding to keep the day from feeling purely transit-oriented.

This closing leg is best treated as a smooth return rather than a challenging ride. It completes the international loop with a practical final approach into the capital.

title: Vosges Ridge and Wine Road Loop
subtitle: A 5-day tour of France

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Strasbourg on D-roads skirting the autoroute, heading south through villages and vineyards to Obernai. The riding is easy but enjoyable, with good pavement, gentle curves, and frequent roundabouts as you pass through Alsatian towns.

Continue along the Route des Vins toward Ribeauvillé on narrow, rolling roads between vines and forest patches. Expect tighter bends, short climbs, and occasional rougher village sections, but traffic is moderate and there are many viewpoints over the plains.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride south on the wine road to Colmar, using departmental roads with a mix of flowing bends and short straights. Pavement is generally excellent, though cobbled old-town zones in Colmar demand slower speeds and careful line choice.

Turn west into the Vosges foothills toward Munster on tighter, more wooded roads. Elevation increases, corners tighten, and visibility can be reduced in forested sections, offering more engaging riding with a moderate technical level.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Climb from Munster up to Col de la Schlucht, a classic Vosges pass with hairpins, sustained gradients, and generally good tarmac. The road is narrower in places, with some exposed bends and potential gravel near the edges, so precise throttle and braking control are important.

Drop down toward Gérardmer on scenic ridge and lakeside roads, mixing mid-speed sweepers with tighter hillside corners. Traffic can be heavier in holiday periods, but line of sight is decent and there are frequent pull-offs for photos and rest.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Spend the day on interconnected mountain D-roads linking Gérardmer, La Bresse, and Bussang. These are narrower, more technical routes with a steady supply of bends, short climbs, and descents. Pavement ranges from very good to slightly patched in shaded sections.

Expect local logging traffic and cyclists on some climbs, requiring disciplined corner entry speeds and good observation. The scenery is constant—forested slopes, ridges, and open meadows—making for a concentrated but rewarding day.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Ride northeast from Bussang toward Saint-Dié-des-Vosges via mid-altitude D-roads with flowing curves and moderate elevation changes. Surface quality is mostly good, and traffic is light outside small towns.

Continue back to Strasbourg on a mix of scenic secondary roads and short faster sections, avoiding prolonged autoroute stints. The final approach is more urban but still manageable, closing a well-shaped mountain and vineyard loop.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Grenoble on the D1091 toward Le Bourg-d’Oisans, avoiding the autoroute and quickly gaining altitude along a valley road with solid pavement and a mix of sweepers and tunnels. Traffic includes cyclists and tourist vehicles, especially in season.

Climb the legendary hairpins up to Alpe d’Huez on a narrow, steep road with repeated tight switchbacks and significant drop-offs. It’s technical but perfectly rideable with good clutch and brake control; descend back to Le Bourg-d’Oisans for the night via the same or alternative local routes.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Continue on the D1091 up to Col du Lautaret, a high pass with wide, well-surfaced sections, open sightlines, and big elevation changes. Weather can be variable, with possible low clouds and cooler temperatures even in summer.

Drop into Briançon on a canyon-like valley road mixing long bends and tighter mountain sections. Watch for roadworks or gravel near the edges, but overall it’s an excellent flowing route for a mid-weight touring or adventure bike.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Ride south from Briançon over Col d’Izoard, one of the great French alpine passes. The climb and descent are full of linked hairpins, varying gradients, and spectacular barren scenery. Pavement is generally good, though there may be patched sections after winter.

Continue to Guillestre on narrower D-roads with more forest, gullies, and tighter radius bends. Traffic is modest, but the road geometry demands concentration, making this a strong day for riders enjoying technical mountain riding.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Head west along lake and valley roads toward Embrun, with a mix of medium-speed sweepers and short, tighter sections near the water. The asphalt is typically good, and the scenery opens to views over Lac de Serre-Ponçon.

From Embrun to Gap, use secondary roads with rolling curves and more moderate elevation changes. It’s less extreme than the high passes, but still engaging and ideal for a slightly easier day while staying off major highways.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Ride from Gap toward Sisteron via scenic D-roads cutting through limestone cliffs and river valleys, with long, flowing bends and intermittent tighter sections. Pavement is good, and traffic is fairly light outside peak holiday times.

Turn back north toward Grenoble using a combination of D-roads and short N-road links, avoiding long autoroute stretches. The final leg is less technical but still varied, finishing a compact but intense alpine loop.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Toulouse on smaller routes skirting the A61/A66, heading toward Foix via rolling hills and farmland. Pavement is good, curves become more frequent, and traffic drops once you’re away from the metropolitan ring.

From Foix to Ax-les-Thermes, the road follows the valley into the Pyrenees, adding elevation, tunnels, and tighter bends. This is a classic access road to higher passes, with a mix of sweeping and sharp corners requiring smooth, alert riding.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride north-west out of Ax-les-Thermes on twisty D-roads that hug the slopes and river, with plenty of linked bends and varied gradients. Pavement is mostly solid, but some steep, shaded sections can retain moisture.

Continue toward Saint-Girons via smaller Pyrenean valleys, where roads narrow and become more technical. Expect a mix of tight, blind corners, short straights, and occasional rough patches, balanced by rich forest and mountain scenery.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Head south and east on mountain D-roads toward Bagnères-de-Luchon, enjoying continuous curves, climbs, and descents. Some sections see tourist traffic, but the road character remains thoroughly motorcyclist-friendly.

Continue toward Arreau through higher Pyrenean valleys, potentially including smaller passes depending on route choice. Expect narrower roads, a mix of hairpins and mid-speed curves, and striking views, requiring sustained concentration.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Ride deeper into the high Pyrenees, possibly skirting famous passes like Col d’Aspin or Col de Peyresourde via adjacent routes. Roads are narrow, climbing and descending repeatedly with changing radii and limited runoff.

Between Saint-Lary-Soulan and Luz-Saint-Sauveur, the terrain is steep and enclosed, with sections requiring a cautious approach due to cliffs, rock faces, and potential loose gravel. It’s demanding but highly rewarding for experienced riders.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Descend out of the high mountains toward Tarbes on valley roads with smoother flow and broader curves, still scenic but less intense than the higher passes. Pavement is generally good, with occasional agricultural traffic near villages.

Return to Toulouse via secondary N and D-roads, avoiding extended motorway use. The final leg is calmer, with gentle hills and frequent towns, providing a well-paced end to a technical mountain tour.

title: Atlantic Coast and Landes Forest Ride
subtitle: A 5-day tour of France

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Nantes on D-roads toward La Roche-sur-Yon, avoiding major autoroutes. The countryside is gentle with good surfaces, broad curves, and light traffic once you clear the urban belt.

Continue to Les Sables-d’Olonne on coastal and near-coastal roads, where you’ll encounter more roundabouts, short straights, and occasional tighter bends near dunes and villages. Wind exposure can be significant near the shore.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride south along the Atlantic edge, using D-roads that parallel the coast but dip inland periodically. These roads are mostly straight or gently curved, but occasional narrow sections and changing speed limits require attention.

Approach La Rochelle and Rochefort via bridges and causeways near marshland, where crosswinds and traffic can be factors. Pavement is generally good, and the scenery features harbors, tidal flats, and low forests.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Continue south through Royan and along the Gironde estuary using smaller coastal roads where possible. Short ferry or bridge crossings and forest corridors provide variety, with mostly easy riding and moderate traffic.

Head toward Arcachon through the Landes forest belt, where long straight sections, sand, and pines define the landscape. Pavement is good, but monotony and possible wildlife crossings mean you should stay alert.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Ride south along the lakes and dunes near Biscarrosse, following secondary roads through forest and lakeside villages. Expect long straights and gentle curves with good asphalt and occasional patches of sand at junctions.

Continue toward Dax on quiet D-roads, with more undulation and curves as you leave the most coastal sections. Traffic is moderate and the road character is relaxed, ideal for a mid-tour day.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Head north-east from Dax to Mont-de-Marsan through mixed farmland and forest on mid-speed roads. Pavement quality remains high, with enough curves to keep the riding engaging without being demanding.

Finish in Bordeaux via a mix of D and N-roads, avoiding the busiest autoroute angles. The final approach is more urban but still manageable, with roundabouts, clear signage, and opportunities to refuel and rest.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Marseille on smaller inland routes toward Aix-en-Provence, avoiding the autoroute network where practical. The roads roll gently through semi-urban and countryside landscapes, with good surfaces and frequent roundabouts.

From Aix to Manosque, ride through increasingly rural Provence, with lavender fields, low hills, and tighter but still moderate curves. Traffic decreases, and the route becomes more enjoyable for steady, rhythm-based riding.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Head toward Valensole on high-plateau roads with expansive views and long, sweeping bends. Pavement is good, but summer heat and tourist traffic near viewpoints may require frequent stops.

Continue to Moustiers-Sainte-Marie, entering more rugged terrain with narrower roads and sharper curves near the Verdon area. Exposure increases near cliffs and gorges, so cornering discipline is essential.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Ride the southern rim road of the Gorges du Verdon, a renowned motorcycle stretch with tight bends, balcony-like sections above the gorge, and varying pavement quality. Some sections are narrow and exposed, so it’s a day for careful, measured riding rather than speed.

Continue toward Castellane on similarly twisty roads, with sustained curves and elevation changes. Traffic can include camper vans and cyclists; good overtaking judgment and patience are important.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Head east toward Grasse on D-roads that weave through foothills and perched villages. Pavement is generally decent, but tight bends, stone walls, and occasional poor sightlines add technical interest.

Turn west and north toward Draguignan, using mid-altitude roads that mix faster sweepers with shorter, tighter sections. The riding is less extreme than around the gorge, but still offers plenty of engaging corners.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Return toward the coast via Brignoles, using secondary roads through vineyards and low wooded hills. The route is smoother and easier, with good asphalt and moderate traffic.

Approach Marseille via inland D-roads, limiting autoroute exposure while still making efficient progress. The final urban section requires attention to junctions and traffic, but closes a highly scenic, varied Provençal loop.

title: Alsace to Germany Black Forest Crossover
subtitle: A 5-day tour of France

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Mulhouse on D-roads through vineyards and small towns toward Colmar, avoiding the A35. The riding is relaxed, with gentle curves, good surfaces, and frequent village speed changes that keep you attentive.

Continue to Sélestat along the Alsatian plain, following secondary routes near the wine road. Traffic is moderate, but the scenery of vines and Vosges foothills makes for a pleasant first day.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Head east from Sélestat toward the Rhine near Marckolsheim on smaller local roads. Pavement is typically good, though some riverbank sections can be narrower and occasionally rough.

Cross into Germany via one of the local Rhine bridges and ride to Freiburg on German B-roads lined with forest and farmland. The curves are mostly moderate, with excellent asphalt and clear signage, making for easy cross-border touring.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Spend a full day in the Black Forest on twisty roads between Freiburg, Todtnau, and Titisee-Neustadt. These routes offer frequent bends, elevation changes, and high-quality surfaces, with some sections narrower and more technical.

Traffic includes local riders and tourists; disciplined speed and cornering technique are important, especially on the popular stretches and in shaded forest sections where grip can vary.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Ride west out of the high forest toward Breisach am Rhein on curving valley and ridge roads that gradually flatten. Pavement remains excellent, and the mix of forest and open views makes for satisfying mid-speed riding.

Cross the Rhine back into France near Breisach and return to Colmar via secondary routes, finishing with gentle curves through vineyards and villages. This is a calmer day after the more technical Black Forest riding.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Complete the loop with a short but realistic ride from Colmar back to Mulhouse, using D-roads through the Alsatian plain rather than autoroute. Curves are gentle, and the road surface is good, making for a relaxed finish.

Although short, this day keeps the route practical, leaving time for rest, maintenance, or additional local detours if desired while maintaining a clear cross-border structure.

title: French Riviera to Italian Ligurian Hills
subtitle: A 5-day tour of France

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Nice inland on the Route de Grasse, quickly climbing into the hills above the coast. Roads are narrower and more curved than the coastal highway, with good asphalt but frequent blind corners and stone walls.

From Grasse to Draguignan, follow D-roads through perched villages and forested valleys, with elevations changing constantly. Traffic is moderate, but the riding is engaging, with numerous linked bends and short straights.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride back toward the Mediterranean near Fréjus, using smaller roads parallel to the autoroute. Expect coastal traffic but also scenic headlands and some twisty inland detours.

Continue east to Menton along the lower corniche or nearby secondary routes, where the road hugs cliffs and passes through tunnels. Pavement is good, but exposure and busy traffic mean careful lane positioning and speed management.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Cross into Italy at the coastal border near Ventimiglia, navigating a mix of urban and coastal roads with roundabouts, short tunnels, and variable traffic. Pavement is generally good, though some older sections may be patched.

Continue to Sanremo on the old coastal road rather than the autostrada, enjoying gentle curves, sea views, and regular town sections. It’s not highly technical but offers classic Riviera atmosphere.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Turn inland from Sanremo into the Ligurian hills on narrow, twisty roads to villages like Dolceacqua and Pigna. These routes are significantly more technical: steep gradients, tight hairpins, stone walls, and sometimes rougher surfaces.

Traffic is light, but the road geometry demands full attention and smooth control inputs. The scenery of terraced hills, rivers, and stone villages makes the effort worthwhile for skilled riders.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Descend back toward Ventimiglia on the same or parallel small mountain roads, again dealing with tight curves and changing elevations. Grip can vary, especially after rain, so a conservative pace is wise.

Cross the border and return to Nice via coastal routes, where the road widens and the ride becomes more relaxed but busier. This final leg offers a clear transition from technical hill riding back to urban coastal touring.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Lille on D-roads through Douai and Cambrai, avoiding autoroutes. The roads here are mostly straight or gently curved, passing through agricultural plains with good surfaces and moderate local traffic.

It’s a gentle first day, with frequent towns, roundabouts, and speed changes that encourage a measured pace rather than aggressive riding.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride east toward Maubeuge on mixed rural and peri-urban roads, with more undulation and curves as you near the Belgian border. Pavement is generally good, though some village sections can be patchy.

Cross into Belgium near Jeumont and continue to Charleroi on regional roads. Traffic increases around the city, but the route remains realistic and manageable for a touring motorcycle.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Ride southeast along the Meuse valley through Namur to Dinant on scenic valley roads. The Belgian N-roads offer good surfaces, medium-speed sweepers, and occasional tighter bends near cliffs and river turns.

Traffic is moderate; passing opportunities are reasonable but require patience behind trucks and caravans. The scenery of river, cliffs, and castles makes this a rewarding day.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Head south into the Ardennes toward Bouillon on more wooded, twisty roads. Elevation changes become more noticeable, and corners tighten, though surfaces remain generally good.

Cross back into France near Sedan, using D-roads through forest and rural valleys. Traffic is light, and the mix of sweepers and tighter sections makes for enjoyable riding.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Ride northwest from Sedan to Valenciennes on a combination of D and N-roads. The terrain flattens, curves relax, and the day becomes more transit-oriented but still comfortable.

Continue back to Lille via secondary roads, avoiding extended autoroute stints. The final urban approach requires attention to junctions and traffic but is straightforward, completing a cross-border Ardennes loop.

title: Lyon to Swiss Jura High Roads
subtitle: A 5-day tour of France

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Lyon on smaller roads heading north-east to Bourg-en-Bresse, skirting major autoroutes. The ride crosses gentle farmland and low hills, with broad curves and good surfaces.

Continue to Lons-le-Saunier on D-roads into the Jura foothills, where curves become more frequent and elevation changes begin. Traffic is moderate, and there are many small towns with roundabouts and speed controls.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride deeper into the Jura, with roads weaving through forest and limestone ridges. The D-roads offer a mix of medium-speed sweepers and tighter bends, with generally good pavement and light traffic.

Approach Pontarlier via scenic river and plateau routes, with modest elevation gains and occasional viewpoints. It’s a balanced day of technical and flowing riding.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Cross into Switzerland near Vallorbe on well-maintained, twisty mountain roads. Swiss routes are typically very well surfaced, with clear markings and a blend of hairpins and sweepers.

Ride north to La Chaux-de-Fonds through Jura high roads, with sustained curves, elevation changes, and forest corridors. Speed limits are strictly enforced, so smooth, controlled riding is key.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Explore a short Jura loop via Le Locle before heading back toward France. Roads remain curvy and scenic, with good tarmac and modest traffic.

Cross back into France and ride to Besançon on mixed N and D-roads, where curves gradually soften and the terrain becomes less rugged. The day balances mountain feel with easier final sections.

days.title: Day 5
days.description:
Ride southwest through Burgundy toward Mâcon, following valley and vineyard roads with gentle bends and good surfaces. Traffic is moderate and predictable, ideal for a steady touring pace.

Continue to Lyon via smaller roads parallel to the Saône, avoiding longer autoroute segments. The final approach is more urban but straightforward, concluding a varied cross-border Jura tour.

title: Normandy Beaches to Belgian Coast Run
subtitle: A 5-day tour of France

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Caen on D-roads toward Bayeux, riding through low Normandy countryside with gentle curves and well-kept pavement. The route passes near historic sites but remains focused on enjoyable, practical riding.

Continue to Saint-Lô on small rural roads that weave through hedgerows and fields. Traffic is light, and the mix of bends and short straights makes for a relaxed first day.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride southwest toward Avranches, including sections near river valleys and low ridges. Pavement is generally good, with occasional narrow stretches through villages.

Turn toward Granville on coastal D-roads, where wind exposure and changing weather can affect riding. Curves are moderate, and the scenery includes cliffs, beaches, and fishing harbors.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Follow the Cotentin peninsula north on coastal and near-coastal roads. These routes offer a mix of straights across open terrain and tighter sections around headlands and villages. Pavement is good but can be exposed to wind and rain.
