From Canazei, climb directly to Passo Pordoi, tackling a dense series of hairpins on a well-surfaced high-mountain pass. The gradients are steep but predictable, and the road is engineered for good cornering lines, though you must watch for buses, cyclists, and loose gravel near the apexes. The descent brings similar technical turns, rewarding precise braking and smooth throttle work.

Loop across Passo Sella, where the road narrows in places and clings to the mountainside with exposed sections and changing radii in the bends. Continue toward Passo Giau, one of Italy’s most iconic passes, combining tight uphill switchbacks, fast open sections, and panoramic views. The final drop into Cortina d’Ampezzo blends flowing curves with busier valley traffic, closing a compact three-day, roughly 350 km route that strings together Lake Garda, Strada della Forra, and the standout Dolomite passes into one concentrated mountain-touring experience.

points.name: Tremosine sul Garda, Strada della Forra

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride north from Tirana through Lezhë and Shkodër before climbing the spectacular SH21 into the Albanian Alps. The road becomes narrow and twisting over the mountains, with steep drops, rough patches, and exposed bends. The final approach to Theth is seasonal and requires extra caution, especially after rain.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Descend carefully from Theth and return through Shkodër before following the Drin valley toward Kukës. The route changes from tight mountain curves to faster rural roads with open views of reservoirs and rugged hills. Watch for livestock, loose gravel, and slow vehicles in the mountain sections.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Cross the quiet northeastern highlands toward Peshkopi on winding secondary roads with sparse traffic and occasional uneven pavement. The route then descends toward the central plain and returns to Tirana. Mountain weather can change quickly, while traffic becomes significantly heavier near the capital.

title: Berat, Gjirokastër, and the Southern Mountains
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Albania

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Leave Tirana through the coastal plain and turn inland toward Berat. The approach follows rolling agricultural roads and low hills, with moderate traffic around Durrës and generally good pavement farther south. Berat’s historic hillside districts and Ottoman houses are worthwhile evening stops.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride through the Vjosa valley toward Përmet and continue across the dramatic southern mountains to Gjirokastër. Expect flowing curves, steep elevation changes, narrow sections, and occasional rough pavement. The scenery includes river gorges, forested slopes, and limestone peaks, while the historic center of Gjirokastër is best explored on foot.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Follow the winding road north through Tepelenë and the Vjosa region before reaching the flatter roads around Fier. The route mixes mountain bends with faster rural highways, and traffic increases near the larger towns. Allow extra time for roadworks and agricultural vehicles on the approach to Tirana.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Cross the central mountains toward Elbasan and continue along Lake Ohrid to Pogradec. The route includes mountain tunnels, sweeping bends, and busy urban sections near Elbasan. The lakeshore road is scenic, with moderate traffic and occasional patched pavement.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Climb to Korçë and continue through quiet roads toward the Albanian side of Prespa Lake. The route then crosses remote uplands toward Përmet, with long curves, open plateaus, and rougher sections in places. Fuel and services are limited, so plan ahead before leaving Korçë.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Ride through the Këlcyrë Gorge and follow the Vjosa valley before turning north toward Berat and Tirana. The gorge road is narrow and winding, with rockfall risk and limited overtaking space. The final stage is faster but more congested around the central plain.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Travel south through the agricultural plain to the ancient site of Apollonia before reaching Vlorë. Most of the road is relatively open and easy, although traffic can be busy near towns. The archaeological park provides a peaceful stop before the coastal riding begins.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Follow the Albanian Riviera over the spectacular Llogara Pass, where tight switchbacks climb through pine forest before descending toward the Ionian coast. The road is paved but can be narrow, exposed, and busy with tourist traffic in summer. Stop at coastal viewpoints above Dhërmi, Himarë, and Borsh.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Visit the Blue Eye before climbing to Gjirokastër and turning north through the mountain valleys. The route contains fast stretches as well as narrow, uneven sections around the southern hills. Expect heavy traffic near Sarandë and Tirana, particularly during the tourist season.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Leave the capital on winding roads through the Mat valley toward Burrel and Peshkopi. The pavement varies from smooth to heavily patched, with frequent bends, forested hills, and very little traffic outside the towns. Allow extra time because overtaking opportunities are limited.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Cross the remote northeastern mountains toward Kukës and continue west across the highlands to Pukë and Shkodër. The road offers reservoir views, forest curves, and dramatic elevation changes, but some sections are narrow and rough. Fuel and roadside services are limited between Peshkopi and Kukës.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Ride south through the coastal plain and climb to Krujë, whose old bazaar and castle sit above the surrounding landscape. The roads are easier and faster than the northern mountain sections, but traffic becomes dense near Krujë and Tirana. Watch carefully for local vehicles, pedestrians, and sudden lane changes.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride north through Shkodër and cross into Montenegro at Hani i Hotit. The Albanian approach is busy and can include unpredictable local traffic, while the Montenegrin road toward Podgorica is smoother and more orderly. Border queues are possible during summer weekends.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Climb through the old royal capital of Cetinje before descending through dramatic switchbacks toward the Adriatic coast. The road offers excellent views but is narrow, exposed, and busy with tourist vehicles. Traffic around Budva and Kotor can be slow in peak season.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Follow the winding Bay of Kotor shoreline through Perast and Herceg Novi before returning inland toward Podgorica. Coastal roads are scenic but often narrow, with frequent pedestrians, buses, and short tunnels. The finish remains entirely in neighboring Montenegro.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Follow the dramatic road through the northern Albanian mountains to Kukës and cross into Kosovo at Morinë. The route includes tunnels, sweeping mountain curves, and open views over reservoirs. The main road is generally good, but trucks, wind, and sudden weather changes require attention.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride across Kosovo’s western plain between Prizren, Gjakovë, and Peja. The stage is relatively easy, with broad roads, agricultural scenery, and mountain views toward the Accursed Mountains. Urban traffic can be lively, and local driving may be more assertive near town centers.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Continue north and east through rolling Kosovo countryside toward Mitrovica and Pristina. The roads alternate between smooth regional highways and busier urban approaches. Finish in Pristina, with the route remaining in neighboring Kosovo for the final stage.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Cross central Albania through Elbasan and follow Lake Ohrid to the Qafë Thanë border crossing. After entering North Macedonia, descend toward Ohrid on scenic lakeside roads. Expect tunnels, mountain curves, and heavier traffic around the resort towns in summer.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride north through the Pelister region toward Bitola and continue across the open Pelagonia plain to Prilep. The roads are mostly paved and flowing, with moderate traffic and broad mountain views. Short rough sections may appear on the smaller roads near the national park.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Follow the Vardar valley north through rocky hills and vineyards toward Skopje. Much of the route is faster than the previous stages, with increased truck traffic and urban congestion near the capital. Finish in neighboring North Macedonia.

title: The Greek Epirus and Meteora Ride
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Albania

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Travel south through Gjirokastër and cross into Greece at Kakavijë. The Albanian section includes mountain valleys and frequent bends, while the Greek roads toward Ioannina are generally smoother and well marked. Border traffic and summer heat can make the long stage slower than expected.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride through the Pindus Mountains via Metsovo, with forested slopes, steep climbs, and flowing mountain curves. The road surface is usually good, although wet conditions and tourist traffic are common in the higher sections. End below the spectacular Meteora monasteries at Kalambaka.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Leave the Pindus foothills and cross the Thessalian plain toward Mount Olympus and the Aegean coast. The route combines scenic regional roads with faster sections near Katerini and Thessaloniki. Traffic becomes heavy approaching the city, so avoid the evening rush if possible.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Follow Albania’s northern plain to Shkodër and cross into Montenegro before reaching the coastal town of Ulcinj. The Albanian roads are busy and sometimes chaotic, while the route beyond the border becomes calmer. Watch for pedestrians, agricultural traffic, and congestion near the coast.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride north along Montenegro’s Adriatic coast, then climb through Cetinje and the rugged interior toward Žabljak. The day features tight switchbacks, exposed viewpoints, forested mountain roads, and significant elevation changes. Some sections are narrow, and high-altitude weather can be cool or wet even in summer.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Cross the dramatic Tara region and descend through pine forests toward Kolašin and Podgorica. The roads are engaging and generally paved, with occasional rough edges, wildlife, and slow vehicles in the mountain sections. Finish in neighboring Montenegro after a scenic highland ride.

title: Lake Ohrid and the Mavrovo Highlands
subtitle: A 3-day tour of North Macedonia

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Leave Skopje on mountain roads toward Tetovo and the Mavrovo National Park. The route climbs through forested valleys and past the lake, with sweeping curves, changing elevations, and generally good pavement. Watch for livestock, slow traffic, and occasional rough sections near mountain villages.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride west around Mavrovo Lake before descending through the dramatic Radika Valley to Debar. The road is narrow and winding in places, with rock faces and limited overtaking opportunities. Continue south toward Struga through rural valleys and enjoy the first views of Lake Ohrid.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Follow the lakeshore to historic Ohrid, then climb over the mountain roads toward Resen and the Pelagonia plain. The final section to Skopje combines open agricultural landscapes with faster rural highways. Traffic increases near the capital, while the lakeside roads can be busy during summer.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride south from Skopje through the Vardar valley and continue toward Prilep across open farmland. The roads are mostly well paved, with long bends and broad views toward Mounts Jakupica and Baba. Stop in Veles or Prilep for historic quarters and traditional food.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Climb the winding road to Kruševo, one of the country’s highest towns, then descend through forested slopes to Bitola. Continue toward Prespa Lake on quieter mountain roads. Some sections are narrow and uneven, and the exposed ridges can be windy.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: The road from Prespa to Ohrid offers peaceful lake views and steep mountain scenery before reaching the busy resort area. Continue through Kičevo and the Treska Valley on a mixture of winding secondary roads and faster highways. Allow extra time around Ohrid and the Skopje outskirts.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Follow the Vardar valley south on a fast but scenic route through vineyards, rocky hills, and broad river landscapes. The main road carries substantial truck traffic, so use caution when passing and near junctions. Gevgelija is a useful base near the Greek border.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Turn east to Lake Dojran, then ride through the fertile Strumica valley toward Berovo. The route becomes quieter and more entertaining near Maleševo, with forest bends and moderate climbs. Pavement is generally acceptable, although patched surfaces and agricultural traffic are common.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Cross the eastern highlands toward Štip and continue to the volcanic hills around Kratovo. Expect a combination of open mountain roads, tight bends, and occasional rough pavement. The final approach to Skopje is faster and busier, especially during weekday afternoons.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride northeast through rolling farmland and the forested slopes toward Kriva Palanka. The road follows a pleasant series of bends beside the Kriva River, with heavier traffic close to Kumanovo. Mountain weather can change quickly in the higher sections.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Make the steep ride to Osogovo Monastery, where the road is narrow and twisting but rewards riders with forest scenery and highland views. Descend toward Kratovo and continue through the rice-growing Kočani valley. Watch for potholes, cyclists, and unmarked bends on the monastery road.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Ride across quiet eastern roads toward Berovo, passing forests, orchards, and open mountain plateaus. The descent to Strumica is smoother and more flowing, while the return through the Vardar region uses faster roads with more traffic. The route is particularly attractive in spring and early autumn.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Head west to Tetovo and climb toward Popova Šapka on a steep, winding mountain road. Higher sections may have broken pavement, loose gravel, and limited visibility in cloud. Descend to Gostivar through the foothills, where traffic becomes denser near town.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: The road through the western valleys offers long curves, wooded slopes, and views toward the Bistra mountains. Continue south to Lake Ohrid, mixing secondary roads with sections of the main highway. Summer traffic near the lake is heavy, but the scenery and historic towns make the ride worthwhile.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Follow the eastern shore of Lake Ohrid to Sveti Naum, then climb away from the water toward Prespa and Resen. The route continues across the Pelagonia plain and north through Veles to Skopje. Lakeside bends are scenic but can be crowded, while the final highway section is faster and less relaxed.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride northeast through Kumanovo and into the wooded Kriva River valley. The route has flowing bends and moderate elevation changes, with heavier traffic near the capital and occasional patched pavement farther east. Kriva Palanka is a practical overnight stop before the border.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Cross into Serbia at Deve Bair, then continue through the mountainous border region toward Vranje. Border formalities and summer queues can delay the day, so carry documents and avoid rushing. Serbian roads are generally good, with forested hills and moderate traffic on the approach to Vranje.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Follow quieter roads through the South Morava valley, with open farmland and low hills framing the route. The ride is less mountainous but still enjoyable on secondary roads around Leskovac. Finish in Niš, where traffic increases and the city center is best explored after parking the motorcycle.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride west from Skopje through Tetovo and Gostivar before entering the Mavrovo highlands. The road climbs through forested terrain and follows the lake with frequent bends. Watch for slower vehicles, livestock, and damp shaded sections.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Descend the dramatic Radika Valley to Debar and continue to Lake Ohrid before returning north on the main western route. The Radika road is narrow and exposed in places, with rockfall risk and limited passing space. Expect more traffic around Ohrid and Tetovo.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Cross into Kosovo at Blace and descend toward Prizren through rolling hills and open countryside. The border road is straightforward, but traffic becomes more active near Prizren. The historic center, Ottoman architecture, and mountain backdrop provide a rewarding finish in neighboring Kosovo.

title: Lakes and the Albanian Riviera Gateway
subtitle: A 3-day tour of North Macedonia

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Travel southwest through the Treska valley and across the wooded interior toward Ohrid. The road alternates between smooth sweeping sections and tighter mountain bends, with occasional rough patches near smaller settlements. Traffic rises sharply around the lake in summer.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Follow the eastern shore of Lake Ohrid to Sveti Naum, then cross into Albania at Qafë Thanë. The lakeside road is scenic and curving, though crowded during peak season. After the border, descend to Pogradec on a generally good road with busy local traffic and broad lake views.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Climb from Lake Ohrid to Korçë and continue across Albania’s high southern plateau. The road features flowing bends, long climbs, and occasional rough or narrow sections, especially around Ersekë. Finish in Gjirokastër, whose steep historic streets are better explored on foot.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Follow the Vardar valley south through rocky hills and vineyards toward Gevgelija. This is a faster stage with some truck traffic, but the surrounding landscape is open and impressive. Use caution on overtaking sections and around the larger junctions.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Cross into Greece at Bogorodica and ride south through agricultural plains toward Edessa and Naousa. The roads are mostly well paved, with gentle curves, mountain views, and moderate local traffic. Keep an eye out for changing speed limits and urban traffic near the Greek towns.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Continue through foothill roads to Vergina, then ride south with Mount Olympus rising ahead. The route combines scenic secondary roads with faster sections near Thessaloniki. Traffic becomes heavy on the final approach, but the mountain and coastal landscapes make this a memorable crossing route.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Leave Skopje through Kumanovo and follow the Kriva River toward the eastern mountains. The road is engaging without being extreme, with forest bends and steady elevation gain. Traffic is heavier near Skopje, while the final section is quieter but can have patched pavement.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Cross into Bulgaria at Deve Bair and continue through Kyustendil toward the forested Rila mountains. The road to Rila Monastery is winding, shaded, and occasionally narrow, with tourist traffic near the monastery. Allow time for border procedures and watch for animals on the mountain roads.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Ride across the Rila foothills through Borovets and Samokov before descending toward Sofia. The mountain roads offer smooth curves, pine forests, and open views, though conditions can be wet or cool at elevation. The final approach to Sofia is urban and congested, so plan to arrive outside rush hour.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Leave Bucharest on the quieter roads toward Curtea de Argeș, then begin climbing into the Făgăraș Mountains. The road to Vidraru follows wooded valleys and reservoir viewpoints, with many bends and occasional rough patches. Traffic is moderate, but expect cyclists, pedestrians, and slow vehicles near the dam.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride the spectacular Transfăgărășan through tight hairpins, tunnels, and exposed high-altitude terrain. The road is usually well paved but can be narrow, wet, and crowded, while the upper section is seasonal and commonly closed by snow outside summer and early autumn. Descend toward Cârțișoara and continue to Sibiu through the foothills.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Cross the southern Transylvanian foothills on a mixture of flowing regional roads and faster valley routes. The scenery changes from Saxon villages and forested hills to the Olt valley and open lowlands. Traffic becomes heavier near Pitești and Bucharest, particularly during weekday afternoons.

title: Bucovina Monasteries and the Carpathian North
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Romania

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride east from Cluj through rolling Transylvanian farmland toward Bistrița and the wooded passes of the Eastern Carpathians. The roads are generally paved and flowing, with moderate traffic around the towns and occasional patched surfaces in the mountain sections. Vatra Dornei is a practical base in a forested alpine valley.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Follow the winding roads through Bucovina, stopping at the painted monasteries of Voroneț and Sucevița. The route passes spruce forests, open meadows, and quiet villages, with generally good pavement but occasional rough edges. Tourist traffic and horse-drawn carts are common near the monasteries.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Ride south through the Moldavian hills before entering the dramatic Bicaz Gorge. The gorge road is narrow, curving, and busy with coaches and roadside vendors in summer. Continue around the red-rock cliffs and forested mountain roads back toward Vatra Dornei.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Leave Sibiu through the Mărginimea Sibiului region, where quiet roads pass traditional villages and rolling foothills. Continue south toward Novaci on a mixture of smooth regional pavement and patched secondary roads. The route is relaxed at first, with increasing curves and elevation toward the Transalpina.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Climb the Transalpina through Rânca and over the high Urdele Pass, Romania’s highest paved mountain crossing. The road offers sweeping bends, exposed ridgelines, and dramatic alpine scenery, but weather can change rapidly and the route is seasonal. Watch for loose gravel, livestock, motorcycles, and slow traffic on the narrow upper sections.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Cross the western Transylvanian foothills via Alba Iulia, Deva, and Hunedoara. The roads alternate between open valley sections and attractive forest bends, with moderate traffic near the cities. Allow time for the historic citadel at Alba Iulia and Corvin Castle in Hunedoara.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Travel north through the Someș valley and the forested foothills of Maramureș. The route includes smooth flowing sections, village traffic, and occasional patched pavement near smaller settlements. Baia Mare and Sighetu Marmației provide useful stops for food, fuel, and local history.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride through the traditional Maramureș valleys, linking wooden churches, farm villages, and the Bârsana Monastery. Smaller roads are narrow and can be uneven, with horse carts, pedestrians, and livestock frequently sharing the pavement. The scenery of hay meadows and wooded hills rewards a slower pace.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Climb from Vișeu de Sus through Borșa and over Prislop Pass into Bukovina. The mountain road has long bends, forested climbs, and some rough or patched sections, while weather can be cool and wet at the summit. Descend toward Câmpulung Moldovenesc and finish in Bistrița.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride southeast from Timișoara through the Banat hills toward Reșița and Anina. The roads become increasingly winding and lightly trafficked, with forested slopes and occasional uneven pavement. Continue to Moldova Nouă above the Danube, watching for blind corners and roadside debris.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Follow the Danube through the dramatic Iron Gates landscape, with limestone cliffs, reservoir views, and a series of engaging bends. Some riverside sections are narrow and exposed, while traffic remains generally light outside the resorts. Finish at Băile Herculane, surrounded by wooded mountains and historic spa buildings.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Leave the Cerna valley and cross the western foothills on broad, flowing roads. The stage is less technical than the Danube route but includes pleasant curves, open farmland, and forested ridges. Traffic increases around Lugoj and Timișoara, especially during the evening commute.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride south through the Transylvanian basin, stopping at Turda and Alba Iulia before reaching Sibiu. The roads combine open agricultural sections with smooth foothill curves and moderate traffic. Urban approaches can be busy, while the historic centers are best visited after parking the motorcycle.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Cross western Romania through the Mureș valley toward Arad and enter Hungary at Nădlac. Much of this day uses faster national roads, with truck traffic and occasional congested settlements, so maintain safe passing distances. Border procedures are usually straightforward, but delays can occur during holiday periods.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Ride across Hungary’s open plains before turning north toward the Bükk foothills and Eger. The roads are generally smooth, with long curves, broad horizons, and moderate traffic outside the larger towns. The final approach to Budapest is urban and congested, particularly during weekday rush hour.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Leave Bucharest for Giurgiu and cross the Danube into Bulgaria on the Friendship Bridge. The Romanian approach is flat and busy, while the Bulgarian roads toward Veliko Tarnovo become hillier and more varied. Expect bridge traffic, trucks, and urban congestion near Ruse.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride south through the Balkan Mountains over Shipka Pass, where forested slopes and tight bends create an enjoyable mountain stage. The pass road can be cool, wet, and busy with tourist vehicles, with occasional rough patches near the summit. Descend through the Rose Valley toward Plovdiv.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Climb into the Rhodope Mountains on winding roads through Asenovgrad, Smolyan, and Devin. The mountain sections are scenic and lightly trafficked, but they include narrow lanes, tunnels, and rough edges. The final route to Sofia is faster and increasingly busy near the capital.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Cross the quiet Banat hills from Timișoara toward Oravița and Moldova Nouă. The route offers forest bends, open plateaus, and light traffic, but pavement can be patched and visibility limited around bends. Fuel and services become less frequent in the final mountain section.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Cross into Serbia at Naidăș and continue through low wooded hills toward Bela Crkva and the Danube. The border crossing is small and may operate more slowly than major international routes, so check opening conditions before departure. Roads are generally paved, with occasional rough sections and quiet rural scenery.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Follow Serbia’s spectacular Danube road through the Đerdap region, with limestone cliffs, reservoirs, and long riverside curves. The road is mostly good but can be narrow near tunnels and exposed sections. Finish in Negotin, remaining in neighboring Serbia for the final stage.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride south through the rolling Moldavian countryside on regional roads connecting Iași, Vaslui, and Bârlad. The landscape is open and agricultural, with gentle curves, village traffic, and some patched pavement. Approaches to Galați can be busy, especially around industrial areas and river crossings.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Cross into Moldova at Giurgiulești and continue through the country’s broad southern plains. Border formalities may take time, and road quality varies from smooth new pavement to uneven or patched surfaces. Watch for agricultural machinery, pedestrians, and limited roadside services between Cahul and Comrat.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Ride north through the rolling Gagauz and central Moldovan countryside. The roads are mostly open and gently undulating, with occasional potholes and active village traffic. The final approach to Chișinău becomes significantly busier, so allow extra time for urban congestion.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Cross the Apuseni foothills from Cluj toward Huedin and Oradea, then enter Hungary near the western plain. The Romanian section offers rolling curves and forested hills, while the Hungarian roads become flatter and more open. Traffic is moderate, with heavier urban movement around Oradea and Debrecen.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride through the northeastern Hungarian lowlands to Tokaj, then turn west toward the Bükk foothills and Eger. The route features long curves, vineyards, open farmland, and generally smooth pavement. Watch for village speed limits, cyclists, and agricultural vehicles on the smaller roads.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Climb through the Bükk hills via Lillafüred and Miskolc, then continue across northern Hungary toward Salgótarján. Forested roads provide pleasant bends and moderate elevation changes, although wet leaves and cyclists can make shaded sections slippery. The final approach to Budapest uses busier roads and urban traffic.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Leave Ljubljana on secondary roads toward Kamnik, passing through the peaceful foothills of the Kamnik-Savinja Alps. Continue through rural valleys to Lake Bled, with smooth bends, moderate traffic, and excellent views of the mountains. The approach to Bled can be busy during summer afternoons.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride through Bohinj and the Triglav National Park before climbing toward Vršič Pass. The pass road has numerous tight hairpins, uneven sections, cobblestone turns, and steep drops, so it rewards a controlled pace. Weather can change quickly at the summit, even in midsummer.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Descend from the Julian Alps toward Bovec and follow the emerald Soča Valley through dramatic cliffs and forested slopes. The road is winding and mostly well paved, with occasional narrow sections and rockfall hazards. Continue through Tolmin and the Idrija hills before returning to Ljubljana.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Head southwest through the forested hills around Vrhnika and Postojna, using quiet roads across the Slovenian Karst. The route has flowing curves, limestone scenery, and generally good pavement, although village streets can be narrow. Štanjel is an attractive historic stop above the vineyards.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride across the Karst plateau and descend toward the coast through vineyards and rocky countryside. Continue along the Slovenian Adriatic to Koper and Piran, where summer traffic and parked cars can slow the final kilometers. Coastal roads are scenic, but expect tight bends and limited overtaking.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Follow the coast north to Izola, then turn inland toward Lipica and the wooded Notranjska region. The route alternates between open plateau roads and pleasant forest bends, with occasional rough patches on smaller roads. Traffic increases near Ljubljana, especially during weekday rush hour.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride west through the forested Idrija hills on a highly entertaining network of secondary roads. The route includes constant bends, steep elevation changes, and occasional narrow or patched sections. Descend toward Tolmin and Kobarid, where the Soča River provides dramatic turquoise views.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Follow the Soča north to Bovec and take the spectacular Mangart Saddle road if it is open. This high mountain road is narrow, exposed, and partly rough, with steep drop-offs and limited passing space; check conditions before riding. The surrounding peaks and views into the Julian Alps are exceptional.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Climb the southern side of Vršič Pass through a sequence of demanding hairpins, then descend toward Kranjska Gora and Lake Jasna. The pavement is generally usable but can be uneven around the pass, with cyclists and tourist vehicles common. The return to Ljubljana combines alpine foothills with faster regional roads.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Travel through Kamnik and into the Savinja Alps on increasingly quieter roads. The final approach to Logar Valley passes forests, alpine farms, and dramatic limestone walls. Some roads are narrow with limited visibility, and the valley entrance may involve a small access fee.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Follow the panoramic Solčava road and continue west through highland villages toward Jezersko. The route features tight bends, forested climbs, and occasional rough pavement, especially on smaller mountain roads. Alpine weather, fallen branches, and farm traffic require a relaxed pace.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Ride through the Poljane and Selca valleys on smooth, curving roads bordered by forests and traditional villages. Škofja Loka offers a worthwhile medieval center, while the roads beyond it remain quiet and technical. The final section to Ljubljana is easier but busier.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Follow the Sava River east through rolling hills and vineyard country. The roads around Litija and Sevnica provide flowing bends and moderate elevation changes, while the valley sections are faster and more open. Watch for tractors, cyclists, and occasional patched pavement.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride north through the eastern wine hills toward Rogaška Slatina and Ptuj. Quiet regional roads climb and descend through vineyards, with generally good pavement and light traffic. Maribor provides a lively historic center and access to the scenic Pohorje foothills.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Follow the Drava valley west beneath wooded Pohorje slopes before crossing the rolling landscape around Slovenj Gradec. The roads are enjoyable and lightly trafficked, with sweeping corners and occasional narrow village passages. The final ride to Ljubljana uses faster roads and becomes busier near the capital.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride north through Kranj and the alpine valley of Jezersko before crossing into Austria at Seebergsattel. The Slovenian approach is narrow and winding, while the Austrian descent is better marked and generally smoother. Expect cyclists, forest shade, and changing weather near the pass.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Follow scenic roads around Lake Wörthersee and continue to Villach before climbing into the Nock Mountains. The route combines lakeside traffic with fast, sweeping mountain roads and well-maintained pavement. Tourist vehicles are common around the resorts, while higher roads can be cool and exposed.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Cross the Turracher Höhe through forests and high alpine meadows before descending toward Murau. The road has flowing bends, good pavement, and significant elevation changes, with occasional cattle near the high passes. Finish in Graz, remaining in neighboring Austria.

title: Emerald Soča to the Italian Alps
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Slovenia

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Cross the western hills via Škofja Loka and Idrija before entering the Soča Valley. The road is a rewarding succession of curves through forests and deep gorges, with occasional rough sections and limited overtaking. Bovec is an ideal overnight base beneath the Julian Alps.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Cross Predil Pass into Italy on a narrow, scenic mountain road beside alpine lakes and fortified historic sites. After Tarvisio, descend through the Val Canale and ride into the Friulian plain. Mountain sections demand caution around tunnels, damp pavement, and occasional rockfall; the Italian lowlands are faster and more open.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Explore the quiet foothill roads of Friuli, linking historic Cividale with vineyard country and San Daniele. The route has gentle curves, good pavement, and lighter traffic than the main Alpine corridors. Finish in Pordenone, entirely within neighboring Italy.

title: Istrian Hills and the Croatian Coast
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Slovenia

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Ride through the wooded Notranjska region and descend toward the Croatian coast at Opatija. The roads around Postojna and Ilirska Bistrica offer smooth curves and forest scenery, while the coast becomes narrower and busier. Watch for wet surfaces in shaded sections and tourist traffic near Opatija.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Follow the eastern Istrian coast and turn inland through rolling limestone hills toward Labin and Pula. The route includes sweeping coastal bends, vineyard roads, and moderate traffic, with generally good pavement. Summer congestion is likely around beaches and the center of Pula.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Cross the Istrian interior on attractive secondary roads between Rovinj and Motovun before returning to the Kvarner coast. The hill roads are curving and mostly smooth, while the approach to Rijeka becomes busier and more urban. Finish in neighboring Croatia with views over the Adriatic.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Follow the Sava valley east and then turn through the forested hills of Dolenjska. The roads are quiet and winding, with vineyard slopes, wooded ridges, and mostly good pavement. Local tractors and narrow village passages can slow progress near the smaller settlements.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Ride through the rolling vineyards of southeastern Slovenia and cross into Croatia at Jurovski Brod. The border road is pleasant and lightly trafficked, while the Croatian section follows broad rural roads toward Karlovac. Traffic increases considerably on the final approach to Zagreb.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Make a loop through Samobor and the wooded hills of Žumberak Nature Park. The roads are narrow, curving, and occasionally rough, with limited services and cyclists on the quieter sections. Return to Zagreb through the western suburbs, where urban traffic requires extra attention.

days.title: Day 1
days.description: Cross Slovenia from the central basin to the eastern wine regions, using secondary roads through Celje, Ptuj, and the Slovenske Gorice hills. The route is mostly smooth, with flowing bends, vineyards, and moderate local traffic. Watch for farm machinery and narrow lanes around the wine villages.

days.title: Day 2
days.description: Cross into Hungary at Dolga Vas and continue through open agricultural country toward Nagykanizsa and Lake Balaton. Hungarian roads are generally easy and well marked, with long curves and broad horizons rather than major elevation changes. Traffic is moderate, but villages often require reduced speeds and careful observation.

days.title: Day 3
days.description: Ride along the northern shore of Lake Balaton through resort towns, vineyards, and rolling volcanic hills. The lakeside road alternates between smooth open sections and busier urban stretches, especially around Balatonfüred. Continue through Veszprém to finish in Székesfehérvár, in neighboring Hungary.

title: Hallstatt to Zell am See Classic
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Austria

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Hallstatt and ride north through the Salzkammergut on scenic lakeside and valley roads. The route combines smooth pavement, gentle sweepers, and short village sections, with frequent mountain views and moderate tourist traffic.
Continue toward Bad Ischl and loop through smaller regional roads near Gosau to keep the ride engaging without relying on major highways. This first day is about flowing alpine scenery, steady cornering, and easing into the trip.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Head west toward the German border and the Königssee area, using mountain roads that tighten as the terrain becomes more dramatic. Expect hairpins, narrow sections, and excellent views of cliffs and turquoise water.
From Königssee, return into Austria and ride toward Hohenwerfen Castle on valley roads with a mix of faster sweepers and steeper approach roads. The castle perch above the valley gives the day a strong landmark stop and a clear alpine-touring feel.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Finish with the Grossglockner as the main event, climbing into one of Europe’s most iconic motorcycle roads. The route is defined by perfectly linked switchbacks, waterfalls, glacier views, and high mountain exposure, with generally excellent asphalt and traffic that can slow around viewpoints.
After the summit area, descend toward Zell am See through a continuous sequence of bends and long alpine views. The final approach into the lake town is calmer and more open, creating a strong ending to a three-day Austria ride.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Begin on the lakes and mountain roads around Hallstatt, then work through the Salzkammergut on scenic regional routes. The riding is smooth and enjoyable, with a mix of lake-edge bends, short climbs, and village entries that keep the pace relaxed.
Continue toward St. Wolfgang and back to Bad Goisern on roads that stay close to the water and mountain slopes. This is a scenic warm-up day with good pavement and frequent photo stops.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride west and north toward the Königssee area on curvy alpine roads with increasing elevation changes. The terrain becomes steeper and more technical, with tighter bends and occasional narrow sections.
Return into Austria via Salzburg’s mountain foothills and continue to Bischofshofen on flowing valley roads. The day balances technical mountain riding with smoother connectors, preparing you for the high alpine highlight ahead.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Enter the Grossglockner route from the north side and climb through a long series of precision-built corners. The road is made for riding: clean tarmac, consistent radii, dramatic drop-offs, and nonstop Alpine scenery.
Use the summit area for the main viewpoint run, then descend toward Zell am See for the finish. The lakeside arrival gives the route a satisfying contrast after the intense mountain section.

title: Tyrol to Hohe Tauern Three-Day Ride
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Austria

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Innsbruck and head east through Tyrol on well-surfaced valley roads with broad curves and strong mountain backdrops. The riding is fast enough to stay interesting, but the roads remain realistic and comfortable for a touring motorcycle.
Continue toward Kufstein and then on to the Königssee area, where the route gains alpine character with tighter bends and more frequent elevation changes. Tourist traffic can be noticeable, but the scenery and road quality make it a strong first day.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride back into Austria and pass Hohenwerfen Castle, a dramatic medieval stop above the valley. The approach roads include medium-speed sweepers and steeper, narrower sections that reward smooth control.
Continue into the Salzburg mountain region toward Großarl on roads that feel increasingly secluded and alpine. This is a day of flowing mountain curves, with some tighter sections and excellent views.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Finish with the Grossglockner as the centerpiece, climbing through a famous sequence of switchbacks and viewpoint turns. The road is purpose-built for the riding experience, with waterfalls, glaciers, and constant mountain exposure.
Descend toward Zell am See for the final stop, where the lake and surrounding peaks create a quiet, memorable finish after two days of strong alpine riding.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Salzburg and head south into the alpine valleys toward Hohenwerfen Castle. The roads are smooth, scenic, and moderately curvy, with a pleasant transition from city edges to mountain country.
After the castle stop, continue to Hallstatt on lakeside and valley roads through the Salzkammergut. Expect gentle sweepers, narrow village entries, and excellent views over water and mountains.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride from Hallstatt toward the German border and the Königssee area, following mountain roads with increasing technicality. The route includes narrow lanes, cliffside sections, and frequent changes in elevation.
Continue back into Austria and toward Bruck an der Großglocknerstraße, the usual staging point for the high alpine road. This second day keeps the ride compact but intense, with strong scenery throughout.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Climb the Grossglockner from Bruck and spend the day on one of the world’s great motorcycle roads. The corners are continuous, the surfaces are excellent, and the views expand with every meter of elevation.
Finish at Zell am See, where the road relaxes into lakeside curves and the pace drops naturally after the alpine effort. The route closes with a clear balance of lake, castle, and mountain highlights.

title: Hallstatt, Grossglockner, and Zell am See Express
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Austria

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Hallstatt and move through the Salzkammergut on lake-side roads that are smooth, scenic, and ideal for settling into the trip. The route features a mix of gentle curves and a few tighter passages through small towns.
Continue west and south toward Zell am See on roads that maintain a relaxed touring rhythm while still offering good alpine views. This first day is the calmest of the three, but it keeps the route visually rich.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Take the Grossglockner as a northbound ride, climbing through a continuous series of switchbacks and panoramic viewpoints. The road is purpose-built for motorcycles and rewards smooth, deliberate cornering.
After the summit section, descend and continue toward Hohenwerfen Castle, where the scenery shifts from high alpine exposure to lower valley roads. This creates a strong contrast within the same day and keeps the route varied.

points.name: Grossglockner High Alpine Road summit area

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Finish with a ride back toward the border and on to Königssee, where cliffs and turquoise water make the road feel especially dramatic. The route remains technical enough to stay interesting but not exhausting.
Return to Hallstatt through the Salzkammergut, ending the trip where it began among mountains and lake views. This final day is shorter and more relaxed, making it a good cooldown after the Grossglockner highlight.

points.name: Grossglockner High Alpine Road summit area

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start beneath Neuschwanstein Castle and follow the Deutsche Alpenstraße through the Bavarian foothills. The route combines smooth sweepers, forested climbs, lakeside bends and frequent village sections, with generally excellent pavement and moderate tourist traffic.
The approach to Walchensee is especially rewarding, with clear water, high ridges and well-surfaced mountain roads. Expect coaches, cyclists and camper vans around the most popular viewpoints, particularly during summer weekends.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride east through the Bavarian pre-Alps on a mixture of regional roads and quieter connecting sections. The route passes forests, farmland and lake country, with broad curves and smooth surfaces that allow a relaxed touring rhythm.
Continue toward Berchtesgaden. Traffic increases near larger towns and resort areas, but the road remains scenic and logically connected, giving you long mountain views before the overnight stop.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Start in Berchtesgaden and visit Eagle’s Nest / Kehlsteinhaus before climbing the Roßfeld Panoramastraße. Access to Kehlsteinhaus is via the Obersalzberg shuttle bus and lift; motorcycles remain at the designated parking area. The Roßfeld road offers broad bends, open alpine slopes and panoramic viewpoints, making it one of Germany’s finest motorcycle roads.
Descend through Ramsau and Hintersee, then finish beside the emerald water of Königssee. The final roads are slower, with visitors and buses around the lake, but the scenery creates an ideal end to this three-day Bavarian route.

title: IT01 — Garda, Iseo and Como Lakes Ride
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Italy

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start on Strada della Forra, the cliff-cut road above Lake Garda with tunnels, rock walls and dramatic views down to the water. Continue through Tremosine and Limone sul Garda, where the roads stay close to the lake and the villages feel like part of the landscape rather than separate from it.
The day is compact but technical, with narrow sections, tourist traffic and frequent photo stops. Pavement is generally good, though the gorge and lake roads can be busy in peak season.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride from Lake Garda toward Lake Iseo, then take the ferry to Monte Isola. The crossing is an essential part of the route, and the island’s fishing villages give the day a slower, more local character.
Continue to Lovere for the overnight stop. Roads around Iseo are smooth but busy near the popular lakeshores, and ferry timings should be checked in advance so the route remains realistic.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Finish through Lake Como with Bellagio and Varenna, where the roads are narrow, scenic and often slower because of traffic and village geometry. This part of the route is more about atmosphere than speed, with villas, ferries and steep lakeside slopes.
Stop at Mandello del Lario to include the Moto Guzzi connection before wrapping up the loop. Expect heavy tourist use on the Como shoreline, especially in summer and around the main towns.

title: SI01 — Julian Alps and Soča Valley Loop
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Slovenia

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Kranjska Gora, with a food stop at Brunarica Kosobrin, then climb Vršič Pass. The road is defined by its 50 hairpins, steep gradients and cobbled sections, making it one of the most iconic mountain roads in the Julian Alps.
Descend into the Soča Valley toward Bovec. The scenery is spectacular and the riding is technical enough to stay engaging, but the narrow road and changing weather require careful attention.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Visit Fort Kluže and then climb Mangart Saddle Road, Slovenia’s highest paved road. The route is short in distance but highly concentrated in difficulty, with narrow lanes, exposed sections and dramatic alpine scenery.
Continue toward Bled via the northern Alpine corridors. The road becomes more open as you leave the high mountain zone, but the scenery remains strong and the driving stays scenic and flowing.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Return via the Julian Alpine ring, linking the turquoise Soča corridor back to Kranjska Gora. The roads are a blend of fast valley stretches and tighter mountain bends, with excellent pavement and frequent places to stop.
Weather can shift quickly in the high country, and tourist traffic is common near the most famous viewpoints. It is a strong final day that ties together the route’s alpine valleys, mountain passes and blue rivers.

title: GR01 — Wild Crete Mountain and South Coast Route
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Greece

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Chania through Therisso Gorge, where the road narrows between the White Mountains and the ride immediately becomes more technical. Continue to Omalos Plateau and use the Samaria Gorge trailhead at Xyloskalo as a scenic point and optional walking stop.
There is no through road for cars or motorcycles across Samaria Gorge, so the route does not enter or pass through the gorge. After the stop near Omalos, continue the next riding stage toward Askifou and the southern coast.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Continue from Omalos across Askifou and descend through Imbros Gorge, which gives the route its most concentrated series of switchbacks. The road is narrow, scenic and very much a mountain route rather than a simple cross-island connector.
Finish at Chora Sfakion on the Libyan Sea. Traffic is light away from the main villages, but the gorge can be sensitive to loose stones and changing weather, especially in shoulder seasons.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Ride the south coast past Frangokastello and Preveli, combining sea-level curves with short inland connectors. The landscape is drier and more open here, and the road feels remote even when the coastline is close.
The final run to Rethymno is more straightforward, but the mix of fortress, monastery and beach scenery keeps the day varied. Expect summer heat, wind exposure and occasional tourist traffic near the major coastal stops.

title: FI01 — Arctic Circle to Utsjoki Lapland Ride
subtitle: A 4-day tour of Finland

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Rovaniemi and head north on the E75 before turning toward Torvinen and Route 962. Continue through Pyhä-Luosto National Park and onward to Sodankylä, where the urban landscape gives way to endless forests, fells and empty northern roads.
The roads are generally wide, smooth and easy to follow, but distances between services increase quickly. Reindeer can appear suddenly on the asphalt, particularly in the early morning and evening, while weather may change rapidly even in summer.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Continue north through Tankavaara and Saariselkä toward Lake Inari and the village of Inari. The route passes through taiga, open fells and long stretches with almost no traffic, creating the vast northern atmosphere that defines Finnish Lapland.
Fuel and food stops should be planned in advance, especially before leaving Saariselkä. The riding is not technically difficult, but monotony, wind, wildlife and large distances require consistent concentration.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Leave Inari and continue through Kaamanen toward Utsjoki and Nuorgam, the northernmost village in Finland. The road follows wide river valleys and open Arctic terrain, with treeless fells and increasingly remote landscapes along the Teno River.
The route remains mostly smooth and flowing, but services are limited and temperatures can drop quickly. Keep the fuel tank topped up and watch carefully for reindeer, especially on open sections with long sightlines.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Finish with a scenic ride from Nuorgam along the Teno River back to Utsjoki. The route offers open Arctic landscapes, low fells, sparse settlements and a powerful sense of distance from the rest of Europe.
This final stage brings the complete route to approximately 940 kilometres over four days. Nordkapp remains an optional continuation from Utsjoki into Norway for riders who want to extend the northern journey.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Cluj-Napoca and head into the Apuseni Mountains through forests and traditional villages. The road gradually tightens and climbs, with a rural feel that is very different from Romania’s famous headline passes.
Reach Padiș Plateau and Belvedere Glăvoaia, where the scenery opens up to forested ridges and wide mountain views. Road quality is variable on smaller sections, so expect patched surfaces and occasional gravel.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Continue toward Cheile Turzii and Rimetea, where limestone walls and narrow valley roads create the route’s most dramatic scenery. The ride is still accessible, but the road surface can change quickly in forested and canyon sections.
Finish in Alba Iulia at the Alba Carolina fortress. The day combines mountain riding with a more historic urban finish, and traffic increases as you leave the highland roads behind.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Use the final day to return through Turda Gorge and back to Cluj-Napoca. This is a more direct riding day, with smoother regional roads and fewer major elevation changes than the previous stages.
The gorge and surrounding countryside still give the route a scenic finish, but the final leg is best treated as a practical return rather than a technical highlight. Fuel and service availability improve as you approach the city.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Glencoe and follow the A82 to Fort William before heading west through Glenfinnan and down to Mallaig. The roads are classic Highland touring: broad scenery, fast-changing weather and a mixture of A-road flow and narrower coastal approaches.
The section to Mallaig is especially good in clear weather, but coaches, camper vans and tourist traffic are common. Ferry reservations should be checked before departure if you are continuing to Skye.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Take the ferry from Mallaig to the Isle of Skye, then ride toward the Quiraing and Neist Point. The roads are narrow, scenic and often slow because of single-track sections, passing places and tourist vehicles.
Skye’s weather can change quickly, and wind exposure is common on the west coast. The day is less about speed and more about constant scenery and careful, patient riding.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Leave Skye and head for Bealach na Bà, one of the most demanding and famous roads in the Highlands. The climb is steep, narrow and exposed, with hairpins and limited visibility that make it unsuitable for inexperienced riders in poor weather.
Continue through Applecross and Torridon to Ullapool on some of Scotland’s best coastal and mountain roads. Expect single-track sections, livestock, rain, and very limited opportunities to overtake safely.

title: NL01 — North Sea, Texel and Friesland Dike Ride
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Netherlands

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Ride from Alkmaar to the North Sea coast at Bergen aan Zee, then continue to Den Helder for the ferry to Texel. The riding is flat and easy, but wind, sand and busy coastal traffic are the main factors to watch.
Explore Texel after the ferry, where the roads through the dunes are quiet and scenic. Because the route depends on ferry times, it is worth planning the day so you are not caught waiting at the harbor.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Cross back to the mainland and ride over the Afsluitdijk, one of the most distinctive long crossings in the Netherlands. The road is straight, exposed and very dependent on weather, especially crosswinds.
Continue to Harlingen for the overnight stop. The route is technically simple, but the dike roads, open horizon and water on both sides give it a strong touring identity.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Ride through the Friesland dike network and fishing villages toward Lauwersmeer. The roads are flat and easy, with narrow shoulders and frequent water views.
The final stage is more about rhythm and landscape than technical riding. Expect weather exposure, crosswinds and occasional traffic near towns and ports.

title: TR01 — Adriatic and Bosnia Seven-Day Grand Tour
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Croatia

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Banja Luka and head toward Una National Park and Štrbački Buk, where the road mixes forest sections, river views and quieter inland riding. This is a good warm-up for the Balkan terrain that follows.
Road quality is variable on smaller sections, and village traffic is common. If you are close to the Bosnia–Croatia border, keep an eye on documentation and local road restrictions, especially around remote river roads.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride past the abandoned Željava Air Base and into Croatia toward Plitvice Lakes. The route becomes greener and more structured, with forest roads, lakes and smoother touring sections.
Continue to Senj as the Adriatic approaches. The road begins to feel more coastal and open, though wind and occasional tourist traffic can be significant near the sea.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Ride the Adriatic coastal road past Karlobag toward Zadar. This is a classic Croatian motorcycle day: sea on one side, mountains on the other, and a long string of bends that reward a steady pace.
Traffic can be busy in summer, and bora winds can make the exposed sections demanding. The road surface is generally good, but you should expect coaches, camper vans and frequent viewpoint stops.

title: HR02 — Hidden Istria Hill Towns Loop
subtitle: A 2-day tour of Croatia

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Pula and head inland into Istria’s hill country. The roads rise through vineyards and stone villages, with smooth but narrow asphalt and a steady sequence of short curves.
Visit Motovun, Grožnjan and Buzet before stopping for the night. This is a culturally rich, low-speed day that fits the hidden-Istria character very well.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride through Hum and Kotli before climbing into the Učka mountains. The route gets steeper and more exposed, with a stronger mountain feel near Poklon Pass.
The descent side offers long views toward the Adriatic. Surface quality is usually good, but forested sections can be damp and traffic can increase near the coast.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Corte and ride through Scala di Santa Regina toward Calacuccia and Col de Vergio. The road is narrow and deeply scenic, with gorge walls, forests and a constant sense of remoteness.
Expect limited passing space, variable pavement and weather that can turn quickly in the mountains. The route is spectacular but demands patience and concentration on the tighter sections.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Move east across Corsica through Ghisoni and the Inzecca gorge before heading to Zicavo. The riding is technical, with narrow roads, repeated bends and strong mountain character.
Road surfaces are generally acceptable, but the terrain is rugged and tourist traffic can appear around the best-known scenic points. The landscape is more important than the pace here.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Finish by climbing toward Zonza and Col de Bavella, where the famous granite spires dominate the skyline. The last day is short but powerful, with steep mountain roads and dramatic scenery.
Weather can shift quickly at altitude, and loose gravel is possible near the edges of the road. This is one of Corsica’s signature motorcycle finales and an appropriate ending to the route.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Lesko and loop past Solina before heading deeper into the Bieszczady Mountains. The roads are quiet and forested, with gentle climbs and long bends that suit a relaxed touring rhythm.
Continue through Cisna and Wetlina. The route is scenic but remote, and the forest edges can feel close to the road, especially where wildlife may emerge unexpectedly.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride east toward Ustrzyki Górne, then continue through Lutowiska and Czarna Górna. This is the quietest and most remote day of the loop, with very little traffic and a strong wilderness feel.
Roads are generally in good condition, but they can be narrow and are often shared with animals, tractors and local traffic. Stay alert for deer and other wildlife, especially in the evening.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Return to Lesko on a shorter final stage that keeps the route realistic after two longer mountain days. The road is less demanding than the forest sections earlier in the trip, but it still offers a pleasant rolling finish.
This closing day is mainly a practical transfer, though the Bieszczady scenery remains attractive throughout. It is a good final stretch before leaving southeastern Poland.

title: CZ01 — Bohemian Switzerland Rock Roads Loop
subtitle: A 2-day tour of Czech Republic

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Děčín and ride along the Elbe toward Hřensko and Janov, where sandstone walls and forested hills define the landscape. Continue through Srbská Kamenice, Jetřichovice and Chřibská before reaching Doubice, Kyjov and Krásná Lípa.
The roads are narrow, winding and scenic, with frequent shaded sections and occasional damp surfaces. Traffic can increase around popular hiking areas, while blind bends, cyclists and local vehicles require a controlled pace.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Continue from Krásná Lípa through Jiřetín pod Jedlovou, Krompach and Jablonné v Podještědí. The mandatory stop is Pekelné Doly, the famous biker cave bar where motorcycles can enter the former sandstone mining complex.
After Pekelné Doly, ride through Česká Kamenice and return to Děčín. The second day combines forest roads, sandstone formations and small Bohemian towns, with generally good pavement but occasional patched sections and slow village passages.

title: IBR01 — Douro Valley to Arribes Border Ride
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Portugal

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Ride the N222 from Peso da Régua to Pinhão and onward through the Douro vineyards. The road is famous for its flowing bends and river views, with terraced hillsides on both sides.
Traffic is usually moderate, but the road can be slower than it looks because of viewpoints, trucks and agricultural activity. It is best ridden with a relaxed pace and plenty of time for stops.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Head east through the Douro Internacional toward Freixo de Espada à Cinta and Miranda do Douro. The scenery changes from vineyards to a much more rugged canyon landscape, with quiet roads and fewer services.
The route is smoother than the mountain roads farther north, but it still feels remote. Cross-border movement into Spain requires normal travel documents, though formal checks are generally minimal within Schengen.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Continue through Arribes del Duero into Spain, where the route stays close to the canyon rim and the roads are light on traffic. The final stretch into Salamanca is more straightforward, but the landscape remains attractive.
This is a well-balanced final day, suitable for finishing a border route without overloading the rider. Surface quality is good overall, though rural debris and tight village corners can appear.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Cangas del Narcea and head into Somiedo on roads that drop into green valleys and climb back into remote mountain country. The riding is scenic and lightly trafficked, with forests coming close to the asphalt in many sections.
Expect wildlife, especially at dawn and dusk, and a generally quiet pace away from the villages. The route is not technically extreme, but it feels wild and isolated.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Climb from Valle de Lago toward Puerto de San Lorenzo and then continue to Puerto de Ventana. This is the route’s high-point day, with mountain passes, open views and a stronger sense of elevation.
The roads are generally good, but fog and rain can appear suddenly in Asturias. Keep a conservative pace through the tighter bends and shaded forest sections.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Use the last day as a short transfer back to Oviedo. The road is less demanding than the previous two stages, but it still offers a pleasant final run through the Asturias hills.
This final stretch is practical rather than spectacular, which helps the route stay realistic after the more remote mountain riding. Weather and traffic can change quickly as you approach the city.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Røldal and cross Saudafjellet on Fv520, a remote high road that can hold snow into the warmer months. The scenery is open and wild, with long views and very little traffic.
Descend toward Sauda past Allmannajuvet and Svandalsfossen, then continue to Sand. The route is scenic and isolated, but weather changes quickly and fuel stops should not be skipped.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride along the Ryfylke fjords toward Hjelmeland and the Songesand ferry terminal. This stage mixes water-level roads with narrow fjord corridors and occasional ferry-dependent routing.
The ferry crossing into the Lysefjord system is a core part of the route and should be planned around the timetable. Once you reach Lysebotn, the terrain becomes more dramatic and more technical.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Climb Lysevegen’s famous hairpins out of Lysebotn, then descend toward Stavanger. The road is steep, narrow and visually spectacular, with tight corners and tunnel sections that require careful speed management.
The final run is a strong closing stage, but it is shorter than the first two days. Expect changing weather, limited overtaking room and a high concentration of scenic viewpoints.
